## Lotus-Leaf Action on Brahman
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 5.10

Who places actions on Brahman, abandoning attachment, and acts — that one is not stained by evil, as a lotus leaf by water.

---

### Devanagari

ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः।

लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा

### IAST

brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ|

lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatramivāmbhasā

### Pratibha Translation

Who places actions upon Brahman, having abandoned attachment, and acts — that one is not stained by evil, as a lotus leaf by waters.

### Pratibha Commentary

The method is twofold and simultaneous: ādhāya karmāṇi brahmaṇi — depositing actions on Brahman — and saṅgaṃ tyaktvā — abandoning attachment — while still acting. The contested image is the lotus leaf: in water, not wet. Engagement without absorption of stain is possible when the metaphysical deposit and affective release coincide. In Vedānta-inflected karma-yoga, Brahman is not an excuse to dump consequences onto the Absolute while clinging privately; the tyāga of saṅga is the seal. Existentially, act inside the wet world without becoming soggy with pāpa-claim. The leaf’s secret is structure, not distance from the pond. Depositing actions on Brahman without abandoning attachment is unfinished consecration; abandoning attachment without the deposit can become dry indifference. The lotus image needs both: contact with the wet world and non-wetting structure. Pāpa-stain is adhesion, not mere proximity to difficulty. Act inside messy necessity with the twin moves until the leaf’s logic becomes your habit. The pond is not the enemy; soaking is.

### Key Terms

**brahmaṇy ādhāya (ब्रह्मण्याधाय)** — having placed upon Brahman -> consecrating deposit of deeds -> more than mood; metaphysical relocation of ownership

**padmapatra (पद्मपत्र)** — lotus leaf -> classic image of non-adhesion amid contact -> purity as non-wetting, not as non-contact

**saṅga (सङ्ग)** — attachment/adhesion -> what must be abandoned for the leaf-effect -> the wetting agent in moral psychology

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Christian “in the world but not of it”:** Structural homology in contact without constitutive capture.
*Divergence:* Christian framing is ecclesial-eschatological in Christ; here the deposit is onto Brahman with explicit saṅga-tyāga.

**Lotus symbolism in Buddhism:** Structural homology in blooming unstained from mud/water.
*Divergence:* Buddhist lotus often figures purity of mind amid saṃsāra; the Gītā ties the image specifically to brahman-deposit of karma.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

Before a messy necessary task, mentally place the action on Brahman, release one adhesive hope or fear, then act — and check afterward whether stain-thinking reclaimed the deed.

---

## Body-Mind Offerings for Self-Purification
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 5.11–5.13

Yogins perform action with body, mind, understanding, and even with the senses alone, abandoning attachment, for self-purification. The integrated one, abandoning the fruit of action, attains steadfast peace; the non-integrated, acting from desire, attached to fruit, is bound. Resigning all actions with the mind, the embodied one sits happily as master in the nine-gated city, neither acting nor causing action.

---

### Devanagari

कायेन मनसा बुद्ध्या केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि।

योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मशुद्धये

युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम्।

अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते

सर्वकर्माणि मनसा संन्यस्यास्ते सुखं वशी।

नवद्वारे पुरे देही नैव कुर्वन्न कारयन्

### IAST

kāyena manasā buddhyā kevalairindriyairapi|

yoginaḥ karma kurvanti saṅgaṃ tyaktvā''tmaśuddhaye

yuktaḥ karmaphalaṃ tyaktvā śāntimāpnoti naiṣṭhikīm|

ayuktaḥ kāmakāreṇa phale sakto nibadhyate

sarvakarmāṇi manasā saṃnyasyāste sukhaṃ vaśī|

navadvāre pure dehī naiva kurvanna kārayan

### Pratibha Translation

Yogins perform action by body, mind, understanding, and even by the senses alone, abandoning attachment, for purification of the self. The integrated, abandoning action’s fruit, attains steadfast peace; the non-integrated, by desire’s doing, attached to fruit, is bound. Having renounced all actions with the mind, the embodied one sits happily as master in the nine-gated city, neither acting nor causing to act.

### Pratibha Commentary

Karma-yoga uses every instrument — kāya, manas, buddhi, indriyas — toward ātma-śuddhi, not toward harvest. The contested contrast is stark: yukta gains naiṣṭhikī śānti by fruit-abandonment; ayukta is bound by kāma-driven fruit-attachment. Then the royal image: the dehin sits as vaśī in the nine-gated city, mentally renouncing all actions — neither doing nor causing. This is not corpse-quietism; it is masterful inhabiting of the body-city without authorship fever. Existentially, purification is the right purpose of technique. If peace is unstable, check fruit-clinging. If authorship fever burns, practice mental saṃnyāsa while the gates still open and close in ordinary life. Multi-instrument action for self-purification relocates the purpose of technique away from harvest. Steadfast peace belongs to fruit-abandonment; bondage belongs to desire-driven fruit-attachment — a clean experimental contrast you can test this week. Mental renunciation in the nine-gated city then describes mastery: gates operate, authorship fever does not. Sit as master of the body-city without confusing stillness for corpsehood. Purification, peace, and non-causing are one curriculum.

### Key Terms

**ātmaśuddhi (आत्मशुद्धि)** — purification of the self -> purpose of yogins’ multi-instrument action -> relocates why one acts

**naiṣṭhikī śānti (नैष्ठिकी शान्ति)** — steadfast/final peace -> peace of the yukta who dropped fruit -> not mood calm; established stillness

**navadvāra pura (नवद्वार पुर)** — nine-gated city -> body with nine openings -> classical image for embodied life under inner mastery

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Marcus Aurelius on the body’s citadel:** Structural homology in inhabiting the bodily post without confusing it for the ruling center.
*Divergence:* Stoic hegemonikon ethics differs from Gītā mental saṃnyāsa toward Brahman-peace.

**Theravāda kāyagata sati:** Structural homology in working with body-gates without ownership fever.
*Divergence:* Satipaṭṭhāna aims at insight into tilakkhaṇa; here the nine-gated sitting is framed as mental renunciation and non-causing.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

Sit for ten minutes as “master in the nine-gated city”: notice doors of sense opening, renounce authorship mentally, then resume one task solely for purification rather than fruit.

## The Lord Creates Neither Doership nor Fruit-Link
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 5.14–5.16

The Lord creates neither doership nor actions for the world, nor the link of action to fruit; it is nature that operates. The all-pervading does not take anyone’s evil or good deed; knowledge is covered by ignorance — by that beings are deluded. But for those whose ignorance of the Self is destroyed by knowledge, knowledge like the sun illuminates that highest.

---

### Devanagari

न कर्तृत्वं न कर्माणि लोकस्य सृजति प्रभुः।

न कर्मफलसंयोगं स्वभावस्तु प्रवर्तते

नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः।

अज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुह्यन्ति जन्तवः

ज्ञानेन तु तदज्ञानं येषां नाशितमात्मनः।

तेषामादित्यवज्ज्ञानं प्रकाशयति तत्परम्

### IAST

na kartṛtvaṃ na karmāṇi lokasya sṛjati prabhuḥ|

na karmaphalasaṃyogaṃ svabhāvastu pravartate

nādatte kasyacitpāpaṃ na caiva sukṛtaṃ vibhuḥ|

ajñānenāvṛtaṃ jñānaṃ tena muhyanti jantavaḥ

jñānena tu tadajñānaṃ yeṣāṃ nāśitamātmanaḥ|

teṣāmādityavajjñānaṃ prakāśayati tatparam

### Pratibha Translation

The Lord does not create doership or actions for the world, nor the conjunction of action with fruit; rather, inherent nature operates. The all-pervading does not take up anyone’s evil or good deed; knowledge is covered by ignorance — by that, beings are deluded. But for those whose ignorance of the Self is destroyed by knowledge, knowledge lights up that highest like the sun.

### Pratibha Commentary

A sharp theological correction: prabhu does not author kartṛtva, karmāṇi, or karma-phala-saṃyoga; svabhāva operates. Vibhu does not collect pāpa or sukṛta. Delusion comes from jñāna covered by ajñāna; when Self-ignorance is destroyed, knowledge sun-lights tat param. The contested claim protects divine non-partiality while assigning process to nature and bondage to ignorance. In Gītā theology this must be held together with earlier theistic activism — a tension productive of depth rather than a simple system. Existentially, stop recruiting God as accountant of your ledger and start destroying the covering that makes the ledger feel like ultimate reality. The sun does not negotiate with night; it reveals what night covered. If the Lord does not create doership, deeds, or fruit-linkage, then recruiting God as cashier of your ledger is already a covering-move of ignorance. Svabhāva operates; vibhu does not take up pāpa or sukṛta as inventory. Delusion is knowledge covered; liberation is ignorance of the Self destroyed until knowledge sun-lights the highest. Stop bargaining with a divine accountant and start destroying the cover. The sun’s work is revelation, not negotiation.

### Key Terms

**kartṛtva (कर्तृत्व)** — doership -> not created by the Lord for the world -> relocates authorship debates into svabhāva and ignorance

**karmaphalasaṃyoga (कर्मफलसंयोग)** — link of action to fruit -> also not Lord’s creation -> challenges crude theistic merit machinery

**svabhāva (स्वभाव)** — own-being/inherent nature -> what actually operates -> the process-field beneath moral theater

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Spinoza’s God without passions or judgments:** Structural homology in an Absolute not taking up human good/evil as a merchant.
*Divergence:* Spinoza’s Deus sive Natura collapses into impersonal geometry; the Gītā still speaks of prabhu/vibhu within a teaching of grace and yoga.

**Madhyamaka / emptiness of agent-action-fruit:** Structural homology in prying apart naive moral metaphysics.
*Divergence:* Madhyamaka empties via dependent designation; here covering-ignorance and solar knowledge of the Self carry the soteriology.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

When you catch yourself making God the cashier of a deed, return to seeing svabhāva operating and ask what ignorance is covering — then seek one clarifying insight rather than one cosmic receipt.

## Minded as That, Gone Beyond Return
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 5.17

Those whose understanding is That, whose self is That, who are established in That, who have That as supreme aim — their stains shaken off by knowledge, they go to non-return.

---

### Devanagari

तद्बुद्धयस्तदात्मानस्तन्निष्ठास्तत्परायणाः।

गच्छन्त्यपुनरावृत्तिं ज्ञाननिर्धूतकल्मषाः

### IAST

tadbuddhayastadātmānastanniṣṭhāstatparāyaṇāḥ|

gacchantyapunarāvṛttiṃ jñānanirdhūtakalmaṣāḥ

### Pratibha Translation

Those whose understanding is That, whose self is That, who are established in That, who take That as highest refuge — their stains shaken off by knowledge, they go to non-return.

### Pratibha Commentary

Liberation’s anthropology is total alignment with tat: buddhi, ātman, niṣṭhā, parāyaṇa — all That. The contested claim is that non-return (apunarāvṛtti) follows when knowledge has shaken off kalmaṣa, not when one merely admires That. Fourfold identification blocks partial spirituality (intellect convinced, life elsewhere). Existentially, inventory the four: what does your judgment track, what do you take yourself to be, where are you established, what is your final leaning? Non-return is not a travel upgrade; it is the end of recycling for a life already unified in That. Fourfold That-alignment blocks partial spirituality: convinced intellect with worldly selfhood, or vague aim without establishment. Non-return follows when knowledge has shaken stains off, not when That is admired from a distance. Inventory buddhi, self-sense, standing, and final leaning as one fidelity. Recycling ends for a life already unified. Apunarāvṛtti is the geography of a completed orientation, not a travel upgrade purchased by belief alone.

### Key Terms

**apunarāvṛtti (अपुनरावृत्ति)** — non-return -> freedom from rebirth-recycling -> the destination of total That-alignment

**jñānanirdhūtakalmaṣa (ज्ञाननिर्धूतकल्मष)** — stains shaken off by knowledge -> purification mechanism -> knowledge as winnowing, not ornament

**tatparāyaṇa (तत्परायण)** — having That as supreme aim/refuge -> teleological orientation of the whole person -> completes buddhi/ātman/niṣṭhā

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**John 17 (being in the Father/Son):** Structural homology in total relational alignment as salvific standing.
*Divergence:* Johannine unity is trinitarian-christological; here tat-alignment is Brahman-ward within jñāna purification.

**Plotinus’ return without return to lower:** Structural homology in ascent that ends cyclic descent.
*Divergence:* Plotinian return is hypostatic; Gītā non-return is framed through shaken-off stains and fourfold That-mindedness.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

For one evening, align all four: think That, sense yourself as That, establish attention in That, and let That be the aim of choices — then sleep without planning a private afterlife reward.

---

## Same-Seeing Across Hierarchies of Form
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 5.18

In a brahmin endowed with learning and humility, in a cow, in an elephant, in a dog, and in a dog-cooker — the wise see the same.

---

### Devanagari

विद्याविनयसंपन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि।

शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः

### IAST

vidyāvinayasaṃpanne brāhmaṇe gavi hastini|

śuni caiva śvapāke ca paṇḍitāḥ samadarśinaḥ

### Pratibha Translation

In a brahmin complete in learning and humility, in a cow, in an elephant, and in a dog and a dog-cooker — the wise are same-seers.

### Pratibha Commentary

Paṇḍita status is measured by samadarśana across a deliberately shocking spectrum: cultivated brahmin, cow, elephant, dog, outcaste dog-cooker. The contested claim is not sociological erasure of roles but metaphysical same-seeing that refuses graded worth of the Self’s presence. In a varṇa-structured world this verse is explosive: learning-humility does not raise ontological value above the śvapāka. Existentially, watch where your seeing upgrades and downgrades beings. If wisdom sharpens contempt, it is not this paṇḍitya. Same-seeing is the ethical phenomenology of the preceding non-dual knowledge. Same-seeing across brahmin, cow, elephant, dog, and outcaste is the ethical phenomenology of non-dual knowledge under hierarchy’s pressure. Learning-plus-humility in the brahmin exemplar already relativizes prestige; inclusion of the śvapāka completes the test. Roles may remain functionally distinct while ontological contempt dies. If your “wisdom” sharpens ranking, it is not this paṇḍitya. Let vision equalize worth before function resumes its work. The contested force of the passage remains practical: it asks for a change in how you inhabit action, attention, and relation — not for ornamental agreement. Return to the line until the claim bites a live decision today.

### Key Terms

**samadarśin (समदर्शिन्)** — same-seer -> one whose vision equalizes across forms -> not sameness of function; sameness of seeing

**vinaya (विनय)** — humility/discipline -> paired with vidyā in the brahmin exemplar -> learning without humility fails the verse’s own ideal

**śvapāka (श्वपाक)** — dog-cooker (outcaste figure) -> extreme of social hierarchy included in same-seeing -> the test case against prestige-spirituality

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Galatians 3:28:** Structural homology in a seeing that relativizes hierarchical identity-markers.
*Divergence:* Pauline unity is “in Christ”; Gītā samadarśana is wise seeing of the same across beings in a Brahmanic frame.

**Mengzi on shared human sprouts — extended:** Structural homology in ethical perception that crosses status.
*Divergence:* Mengzi focuses human moral potentials; this verse explicitly includes animals and the socially abjected in same-seeing.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

Meet three beings today across your private hierarchy (esteemed, ordinary, despised) and practice one minute of same-seeing before any useful/role evaluation returns.

---

## Even Here Creation Is Conquered
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 5.19–5.21

Even here creation is conquered by those whose mind is established in equality; for Brahman is faultless and equal, therefore they are established in Brahman. One should not rejoice on obtaining the pleasant nor tremble on obtaining the unpleasant; with firm understanding, unconfused, the Brahman-knower is established in Brahman. Whose self is unattached to outer contacts finds the happiness that is in the Self; that one, yoked in Brahman-yoga, enjoys imperishable happiness.

---

### Devanagari

इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः।

निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद्ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः

न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम्।

स्थिरबुद्धिरसम्मूढो ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मणि स्थितः

बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम्।

स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते

### IAST

ihaiva tairjitaḥ sargo yeṣāṃ sāmye sthitaṃ manaḥ|

nirdoṣaṃ hi samaṃ brahma tasmādbrahmaṇi te sthitāḥ

na prahṛṣyetpriyaṃ prāpya nodvijetprāpya cāpriyam|

sthirabuddhirasammūḍho brahmavidbrahmaṇi sthitaḥ

bāhyasparśeṣvasaktātmā vindatyātmani yatsukham|

sa brahmayogayuktātmā sukhamakṣayamaśnute

### Pratibha Translation

Even here creation is conquered by those whose mind stands in equality; for Brahman is faultless and equal — therefore they stand in Brahman. Let one not exult on obtaining the dear, nor tremble on obtaining the undear; firm in understanding, unconfused, the Brahman-knower stands in Brahman. Whose self is unattached in outer contacts finds the happiness that is in the Self; yoked in Brahman-yoga, that one enjoys undying happiness.

### Pratibha Commentary

Ihaiva — even here — sarga is conquered by sāmya-sthita mind, because Brahman itself is nirdoṣa and sama. The contested claim collapses the postponement of liberation to afterlife geography: establishment in equality is establishment in Brahman now. Emotional discipline follows: no praharṣa at priya, no udvega at apriya. Then the happiness shift: unattached to bāhya-sparśa, one finds ātman-sukha and, through brahma-yoga, akṣaya sukha. Existentially, equality is not blandness; it is ontological fidelity to Brahman’s own sameness. If contact-happiness still rules, creation still conquers you. If Self-happiness is found, even here the revolving show has lost its final claim. Conquering creation even here means the revolving show loses final claim over a mind established in equality. Brahman’s own faultless sameness is the template; exultation and trembling at contacts are refusals of that template. Happiness then shifts inward through non-attachment to outer touches, ripening into undying joy via Brahman-yoga. Postpone-nothing liberation is the verse’s dare. If timed contacts still define your joy, creation still conquers you.

### Key Terms

**sāmya (साम्य)** — equality/evenness -> mind’s standing that conquers creation here -> mirrors Brahman’s own sama nature

**bāhyasparśa (बाह्यस्पर्श)** — outer contact -> sensory-world touching that falsely monopolizes sukha -> the field of non-attachment

**akṣaya sukha (अक्षय सुख)** — undying happiness -> fruit of brahma-yoga yoking -> against perishable contact-pleasures

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Epictetus on preferred indifferents:** Structural homology in refusing exultation/trembling at externals.
*Divergence:* Stoic frame is prohairesis and logos; here equality establishes one in Brahman and yields undying Self-happiness.

**Augustine on restless heart:** Structural homology in redirecting joy from outer contacts to the true ground.
*Divergence:* Augustine’s rest is in God through Christ; the Gītā names brahma-vid establishment and brahma-yoga.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

On the next pleasant and unpleasant message, withhold exultation and trembling for thirty seconds; turn attention to evenness and look for a quieter happiness that does not depend on the contact.

---

## Contact-Born Joys Are Wombs of Pain
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 5.22–5.24

The enjoyments born of contact are only wombs of pain; they have beginning and end, Kaunteya — the wise one does not rejoice in them. Who can endure here, before release from the body, the urge born of desire and anger — that one is integrated, that one is a happy human. Who has happiness within, delight within, and likewise light within — that yogin becomes Brahman and attains Brahman-nirvāṇa.

---

### Devanagari

ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते।

आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः

शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात्।

कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः

योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः।

स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति

### IAST

ye hi saṃsparśajā bhogā duḥkhayonaya eva te|

ādyantavantaḥ kaunteya na teṣu ramate budhaḥ

śaknotīhaiva yaḥ soḍhuṃ prākśarīravimokṣaṇāt|

kāmakrodhodbhavaṃ vegaṃ sa yuktaḥ sa sukhī naraḥ

yo'ntaḥsukho'ntarārāmastathāntarjyotireva yaḥ|

sa yogī brahmanirvāṇaṃ brahmabhūto'dhigacchati

### Pratibha Translation

For the enjoyments born of contact are only wombs of pain; they have beginning and end, Kaunteya — the wise one does not delight in them. Who is able, even here, before release from the body, to endure the surge born of desire and anger — that one is integrated, that one is a happy human. Who is happy within, delighting within, and likewise light within — that yogin, become Brahman, attains Brahman-nirvāṇa.

### Pratibha Commentary

Contact-born bhogas are not mild distractions; they are duḥkha-yonayaḥ — wombs of pain — because they are ādyanta-vat, timed things. The contested happiness criterion is endurance: who can bear, before death, the vega of kāma-krodha is already yukta and sukhī. Then the interior trinity — antaḥ-sukha, antar-ārāma, antar-jyotis — marks the yogin who, brahma-bhūta, reaches brahma-nirvāṇa. In the Gītā’s late chapter-5 ascent, nirvāṇa-language enters a Brahmanic key. Existentially, stop calling surge-management “repression” when it is the doorway of happiness, and stop calling timed pleasures “life” when they gestate pain. The real festival is inward light. Calling contact-joys wombs of pain is not anti-life; it is obstetric honesty about what timed pleasures gestate. Enduring kāma-krodha’s surge before death is already happiness and integration — a criterion that relocates “the happy human” from entertainment to capacity. Inward happiness, delight, and light then mark the yogin who becomes Brahman and attains Brahman-nirvāṇa. The festival moves inside. Surge-endurance is the doorway, not a denial of joy.

### Key Terms

**duḥkhayoni (दुःखयोनि)** — womb of pain -> contact-enjoyment as generative source of suffering -> stronger than “leads to pain”

**vega (वेग)** — surge/impulse -> kāma-krodha’s force to be endured -> names kinetic affliction, not abstract vice

**brahmanirvāṇa (ब्रह्मनिर्वाण)** — Brahman-nirvāṇa -> extinction/bliss-attainment in Brahman idiom -> cross-traditional term re-keyed to brahma-bhūta

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Buddha’s First Noble Truth / vedanā analysis:** Structural homology in contact-feeling as structurally painful in its timed nature.
*Divergence:* Early Buddhism aims at nibbāna via path without ātman/Brahman; here endurance and inward light culminate in brahmanirvāṇa.

**Evagrius on enduring logismoi:** Structural homology in happiness tied to enduring passionate surges before death.
*Divergence:* Evagrian goal is apatheia in prayer; the Gītā’s goal is brahma-bhūta attainment of brahmanirvāṇa.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

When a contact-pleasure calls, label it “timed womb of pain,” endure one kāma or krodha surge without acting it out, and rest attention in inward happiness-light for one minute.

---

## Seers of Brahman-Nirvāṇa, Gates of Breath
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 5.25–5.27

Seers whose stains are thinned, whose doubts are cut, who are self-restrained and delight in the welfare of all beings, obtain Brahman-nirvāṇa. For ascetics free from desire and anger, with mind restrained, who know the Self — Brahman-nirvāṇa lies near on every side. Shutting out outer contacts, fixing the gaze between the brows, equalizing in-breath and out-breath moving within the nostrils—

---

### Devanagari

लभन्ते ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृषयः क्षीणकल्मषाः।

छिन्नद्वैधा यतात्मानः सर्वभूतहिते रताः

कामक्रोधवियुक्तानां यतीनां यतचेतसाम्।

अभितो ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं वर्तते विदितात्मनाम्

स्पर्शान्कृत्वा बहिर्बाह्यांश्चक्षुश्चैवान्तरे भ्रुवोः।

प्राणापानौ समौ कृत्वा नासाभ्यन्तरचारिणौ

### IAST

labhante brahmanirvāṇamṛṣayaḥ kṣīṇakalmaṣāḥ|

chinnadvaidhā yatātmānaḥ sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ

kāmakrodhaviyuktānāṃ yatīnāṃ yatacetasām|

abhito brahmanirvāṇaṃ vartate viditātmanām

sparśānkṛtvā bahirbāhyāṃścakṣuścaivāntare bhruvoḥ|

prāṇāpānau samau kṛtvā nāsābhyantaracāriṇau

### Pratibha Translation

Seers whose stains are thinned, whose doubleness is cut, who are self-restrained, who delight in the welfare of all beings, obtain Brahman-nirvāṇa. For ascetics parted from desire and anger, with mind restrained, who have known the Self — Brahman-nirvāṇa is present all around. Making outer contacts outward, fixing the eyes at the brow’s center, making prāṇa and apāna equal as they move within the nose—

### Pratibha Commentary

Brahman-nirvāṇa is not only an interior trophy; it is obtained by ṛṣis whose kalmaṣa is thinned, whose dvaidha is cut, who are yata-ātman and delight in sarva-bhūta-hita. The contested social edge is essential: same-seeing ripens into welfare-delight, not into cold detachment. For yatins free of kāma-krodha, with known Self, brahmanirvāṇa “lies all around” (abhitaḥ) — proximity language against distant heaven-thinking. Then technique begins: exclude outer contacts, gaze between brows, equalize breaths in the nostrils. Existentially, ethics and breath are one curriculum. Without welfare-delight and cut doubt, brow-gazing is cosmetics. With them, the end is already near. Welfare-delight joins cut doubt and thinned stain so that Brahman-nirvāṇa cannot be mistaken for private escape. For Self-knowers free of desire-anger, that end “lies all around,” collapsing distance-spirituality. Technique — outer contacts outward, brow gaze, equalized breaths — arrives only after this ethical-cognitive profile. Without it, psychosomatic methods are cosmetics. With it, breath and compassion are one readiness.

### Key Terms

**chinnadvaidha (छिन्नद्वैध)** — whose doubleness/doubt is cut -> unresolved split removed -> pairs with earlier saṃśaya-cutting

**sarvabhūtahita (सर्वभूतहित)** — welfare of all beings -> delight-field of the seers -> blocks nirvāṇa as private escape

**abhitaḥ (अभितः)** — all around/near on every side -> brahmanirvāṇa’s proximity for the Self-knowers -> spatial metaphor for readiness

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Bodhisattva synthesis of śamatha and karuṇā:** Structural homology in concentration joined to welfare of beings.
*Divergence:* Bodhisattva vow postpones final extinguishing for others; here seers obtain brahmanirvāṇa while characterized by welfare-delight.

**Hesychast psychosomatic prayer (gaze, breath):** Structural homology in coordinating eyes and breath for interior stillness.
*Divergence:* Hesychasm invokes the Name; the Gītā’s sequence is Brahmanic-yogic toward brahmanirvāṇa.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

Do one act for another being’s welfare, then sit: sense contacts outward, rest gaze softly toward the brow center, and equalize inhale and exhale for twenty breaths.

---

## Freed Always; Knowing the Friend of All
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 5.28–5.29

With senses, mind, and understanding restrained, the sage whose highest aim is liberation, from whom desire, fear, and anger have departed — that one is always freed indeed. Knowing me as the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, the great lord of all worlds, the friend of all beings — one reaches peace.

---

### Devanagari

यतेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिर्मुनिर्मोक्षपरायणः।

विगतेच्छाभयक्रोधो यः सदा मुक्त एव सः

भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम्।

सुहृदं सर्वभूतानां ज्ञात्वा मां शान्तिमृच्छति

### IAST

yatendriyamanobuddhirmunirmokṣaparāyaṇaḥ|

vigatecchābhayakrodho yaḥ sadā mukta eva saḥ

bhoktāraṃ yajñatapasāṃ sarvalokamaheśvaram|

suhṛdaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ jñātvā māṃ śāntimṛcchati

### Pratibha Translation

With senses, mind, and understanding restrained, the sage intent on liberation as highest aim, from whom wish, fear, and anger have gone — that one is always liberated indeed. Knowing me as the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, the great lord of all worlds, the friend of all beings — one reaches peace.

### Pratibha Commentary

Chapter 5 seals with a double climax: the muni whose instruments are restrained, aimed at mokṣa, emptied of icchā-bhaya-krodha, is sadā mukta — always free, not free later. Then theistic knowing: Krishna as bhoktṛ of yajña and tapas, maheśvara of all worlds, suhṛd of all beings — knowing him thus, one reaches śānti. The contested weave is crucial: impersonal brahmanirvāṇa pedagogy culminates in recognizing a personal friend-lord who enjoys offerings without ceasing to be friend of all. Existentially, freedom’s marks are affective (wish-fear-anger gone) and relational (knowing the Friend). Peace is not only extinguished surge; it is recognition of the One who receives austerity and still befriends every being. Always-free is present tense for the restrained sage aimed at liberation with wish-fear-anger gone — freedom as standing, not postponement. Peace then arrives through knowing Krishna as enjoyer of offerings, lord of worlds, and friend of all beings. Sovereignty and friendship together prevent both cold metaphysics and sentimental piety. Chapter 5’s impersonal and personal pedagogies seal each other. Recognize the Friend who receives austerity without ceasing to befriend every being.

### Key Terms

**sadā mukta (सदा मुक्त)** — always liberated -> freedom as present standing of the restrained sage -> against postponed salvation fantasy

**suhṛd (सुहृद्)** — friend/good-hearted one -> Krishna as friend of all beings -> softens pure sovereignty into companionship

**bhoktṛ (भोक्तृ)** — enjoyer/consumer of offerings -> the Lord as recipient of yajña-tapas -> completes the sacrificial arc of chapters 3–5

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Bhakti climax after jñāna (e.g., later Gītā chapters):** Structural homology in knowledge ripening into personal recognition.
*Divergence:* Here the recognition is compressed into suhṛd-maheśvara knowing as peace’s door at chapter’s end.

**Jesus as lord and friend (John 15):** Structural homology in sovereignty joined to friendship as the relational seal of peace.
*Divergence:* Christian friendship is covenantal in Christ; the Gītā’s suhṛd is enjoyer of sacrifice and lord of worlds within yoga’s mokṣa aim.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

Restrain speech-driven wish, fear, and anger for one conversation; then recollect the Lord as friend of all beings — including your opponent — and end in peace without needing to win.

## Renouncer Is Not the Fireless Idle
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 6.1–6.3

The Blessed Lord said: Who does the action that must be done without depending on action’s fruit — that one is a renouncer and a yogin, not the one without fire and not the inactive. What they call renunciation, know that as yoga, Pāṇḍava; for no one becomes a yogin without renouncing intention. For the sage wishing to ascend to yoga, action is said to be the means; for the same one who has ascended to yoga, stillness is said to be the means.

---

### Devanagari

श्री भगवानुवाच

अनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः।

स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः

यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव।

न ह्यसंन्यस्तसङ्कल्पो योगी भवति कश्चन

आरुरुक्षोर्मुनेर्योगं कर्म कारणमुच्यते।

योगारूढस्य तस्यैव शमः कारणमुच्यते

### IAST

śrī bhagavānuvāca

anāśritaḥ karmaphalaṃ kāryaṃ karma karoti yaḥ|

sa saṃnyāsī ca yogī ca na niragnirna cākriyaḥ

yaṃ saṃnyāsamiti prāhuryogaṃ taṃ viddhi pāṇḍava|

na hyasaṃnyastasaṅkalpo yogī bhavati kaścana

ārurukṣormuneryogaṃ karma kāraṇamucyate|

yogārūḍhasya tasyaiva śamaḥ kāraṇamucyate

### Pratibha Translation

The Blessed Lord said: Who performs the action that must be done without depending on the fruit of action — that one is a renouncer and a yogin — not the fireless one, and not the inactive. What they call renunciation, know as yoga, Pāṇḍava; for no one becomes a yogin without having renounced intention [saṅkalpa]. For the sage wishing to climb to yoga, action is said to be the means; for that same one who has climbed to yoga, stillness [śama] is said to be the means.

### Pratibha Commentary

Chapter 6 opens by collapsing false images of holiness: neither niragni nor akrīya defines saṃnyāsa/yoga. The contested identity is positive — do kārya without āśraya on fruit — and then conceptual: saṃnyāsa is yoga because without renounced saṅkalpa no one is a yogin. Stage-theory follows: for the ārurukṣu, karma is the means; for the yogārūḍha, śama is the means. In pedagogical yoga this prevents beginners from aping the stillness of the ascended, and prevents the ascended from clinging to beginner activism as identity. Existentially, locate your stage honestly. If you still need climbing, act without fruit-dependence; if you have climbed, let stillness be means without contempt for those still acting. Costume without stage-fit is failure. Stage-fit saves practice from costume. Beginners aping stillness skip the karma that climbs; the ascended clinging to activism refuse the śama that is now their means. Saṅkalpa-renunciation is the common root that makes both stages yoga rather than career choices. Neither fireless inactivity nor fruit-dependent work earns the names renouncer and yogin. Locate your stage, then use the means that actually belong to it.

### Key Terms

**niragni (निरग्नि)** — without (sacrificial) fire -> false emblem of renunciation -> ritual absence mistaken for yoga

**saṅkalpa (सङ्कल्प)** — formative intention/resolve -> what must be renounced to be a yogin -> deeper than quitting tasks

**yogārūḍha (योगारूढ)** — one who has ascended to yoga -> stage where śama becomes the means -> marks a real transition of method

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**John of the Cross on active vs passive nights:** Structural homology in different means proper to different stages of ascent.
*Divergence:* Carmelite staging is christological-mystical; the Gītā stages karma then śama under saṅkalpa-renunciation.

**Confucian graded learning vs quiet sitting debates:** Structural homology in refusing premature stillness as moral excellence.
*Divergence:* Confucian framing is ritual-moral cultivation; here stillness is explicitly the means of the already yoga-ascended.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

Decide whether you are climbing or ascended for today: if climbing, complete one necessary action without leaning on its fruit; if ascended, take one period of deliberate stillness without using it to judge actors.

---

## When Nothing Clings, Yoga Has Ascended
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 6.4

When one no longer clings to sense-objects or to actions, having renounced all intentions — then one is said to have ascended to yoga.

---

### Devanagari

यदा हि नेन्द्रियार्थेषु न कर्मस्वनुषज्जते।

सर्वसङ्कल्पसंन्यासी योगारूढस्तदोच्यते

### IAST

yadā hi nendriyārtheṣu na karmasvanuṣajjate|

sarvasaṅkalpasaṃnyāsī yogārūḍhastadocyate

### Pratibha Translation

For when one does not cling to sense-objects or to actions, renouncer of all intentions — then one is called yoga-ascended.

### Pratibha Commentary

The definition of yogārūḍha is negative-positive: non-clinging to indriyārtha and to karmas, plus total saṅkalpa-saṃnyāsa. The contested clarity is diagnostic — ascent is not measured by hours seated but by the end of anuṣaṅga (adhesive following) toward objects and deeds, and by the emptying of formative resolves. In yoga psychology this is liberation’s behavioral signature inside ordinary life. Existentially, inventory cling-points: which objects, which projects, which resolutions still own you? When those adhesives release, you may use the name yogārūḍha without fraud. Non-clinging to objects and actions plus total intention-renunciation is a public-private definition of ascent: visible adhesives and invisible resolves both release. Hours on a seat cannot override anuṣaṅga that still owns your projects. The name yogārūḍha is honest only when the cling-inventory is empty. Let that inventory, not your self-branding, decide whether stillness is yet your proper means. The contested force of the passage remains practical: it asks for a change in how you inhabit action, attention, and relation — not for ornamental agreement. Return to the line until the claim bites a live decision today.

### Key Terms

**anuṣajjate (अनुषज्जते)** — clings/follows adhesively -> the verb whose cessation marks ascent -> more precise than “likes”

**sarvasaṅkalpasaṃnyāsī (सर्वसङ्कल्पसंन्यासी)** — renouncer of all intentions -> comprehensive dropping of formative resolve -> the positive content of ascent

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Zen “no dwelling” (Diamond Sūtra echoes):** Structural homology in non-abiding amid objects and acts.
*Divergence:* Zen non-abiding is emptiness-flavored; here non-clinging is definitional of yogārūḍha within Gītā staging.

**Stoic release of hormē toward externals:** Structural homology in ending adhesive impulse toward things and outcomes.
*Divergence:* Stoicism retains rational assent structure; the Gītā centers total saṅkalpa-renunciation as yoga-ascent.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

List three current saṅkalpas; release one completely for twenty-four hours and watch whether sense-objects and tasks lose their adhesive pull.

---

## Lift the Self by the Self
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 6.5

One should lift the self by the Self, and not degrade the self; for the self alone is the self’s friend, and the self alone is the self’s enemy.

---

### Devanagari

उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत्।

आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः

### IAST

uddharedātmanā''tmānaṃ nātmānamavasādayet|

ātmaiva hyātmano bandhurātmaiva ripurātmanaḥ

### Pratibha Translation

One should raise the self by the Self, and should not cause the self to sink; for the self alone is friend of the self, and the self alone is enemy of the self.

### Pratibha Commentary

Responsibility returns inward with shocking symmetry: uplift and degradation are both self-to-self relations. The contested claim refuses permanent outsourcing of salvation or blame — ātman alone is bandhu and ripu. In yogic ethics this is empowerment without narcissism: the same “self” that sabotages can be the instrument of raising, and the deeper Self is the lever. Existentially, notice the moment you treat yourself as helpless victim of yourself while still choosing the sinking move. The verse commands uddharet — lift — and forbids avasādayet — do not sink yourself. Friendship with yourself is an achievement of discipline, not a feeling. Self-as-friend and self-as-enemy refuse permanent outsourcing of either blame or rescue. The same agency that chooses sinking can choose lifting; the deeper Self is the lever of uplift. This is discipline’s empowerment, not pep talk. Notice the moment you rehearse helplessness while still selecting the degrading move. Friendship with yourself is built by the lift you actually perform.

### Key Terms

**uddharet (उद्धरेत्)** — should lift up -> imperative of self-raising -> agency located in self-Self relation

**avasādayet (अवसादयेत्)** — should sink/depress -> the forbidden self-sabotage -> names degradation as active

**bandhu / ripu (बन्धु / रिपु)** — friend / enemy -> twin roles the self plays toward itself -> moral psychology as interior alliance or war

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Epictetus on self-responsibility of prohairesis:** Structural homology in locating friend/enemy in one’s own governing choices.
*Divergence:* Stoic hegemonikon differs from Gītā’s ātman/Self double play toward yoga uplift.

**Hasidic “working on oneself”:** Structural homology in refusing to leave the inner enemy unconfronted.
*Divergence:* Hasidic work is God-relational within mitsvot; here the formula is terse Self-by-self uplift for yoga.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

Catch one self-sinking move (rumination, spite, indulgence); interrupt it with one concrete self-raising act chosen as friendship, not as punishment.

## Conquered Self Is Friend; Unconquered Is Foe
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 6.6

The self is friend to that self by whom the self itself has been conquered; but for the unconquered self, the self would stand in enmity like an enemy.

---

### Devanagari

बन्धुरात्माऽऽत्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः।

अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत्

### IAST

bandhurātmā''tmanastasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ|

anātmanastu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat

### Pratibha Translation

The self is a friend to the self of one by whom the self has been conquered by the self; but for the one without self-mastery, the self would operate in enmity — the self itself like an enemy.

### Pratibha Commentary

Friendship with oneself is conditional on jita — conquest of self by self. The contested severity is that without mastery (anātman here as unmastered person), the self behaves as enemy. This is not self-hatred theology; it is diagnostic of interior civil war when discipline fails. In yoga, “self” is both the field to be conquered and the conqueror — a reflexive martial ethics. Existentially, if your impulses systematically ambush your aims, you do not need a new enemy outside; you need conquest that turns the inner actor into bandhu. Until then, expect sabotage from the nearest agent: you. Conditional friendship means mastery transforms the inner relation: conquered self becomes bandhu; unmastered self operates like an enemy. Interior civil war is then not mysterious fate but the predictable climate of non-conquest. Yoga’s reflexive martial ethics — self conquering self — aims at alliance, not at self-hatred. If impulses ambush aims, the nearest enemy is already in the house. Conquer once today and feel the alliance begin.

### Key Terms

**jitātman (implied जित)** — conquered self -> condition for self-friendship -> mastery as relational transformation

**anātman (अनात्मन्)** — here: one lacking self-possession/mastery -> not metaphysical non-self doctrine in this verse’s use -> practical unmastered person

**śatruvat (शत्रुवत्)** — like an enemy -> simile for unmastered self’s operation -> makes interior conflict vivid

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Plato’s Republic (city-soul justice as inner rule):** Structural homology in friendship/peace requiring right rule within.
*Divergence:* Plato’s parts are logistikon/thumos/epithumia; the Gītā compresses to self-conquest by self for yoga.

**Freud’s structural conflict (popularly):** Structural homology in self opposed to itself.
*Divergence:* Psychoanalysis theorizes unconscious agencies; Krishna commands conquest as yogic ethical task.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

Choose one recurrent self-enemy behavior; conquer it once today by a pre-decided counter-act, and note the shift from enmity toward friendship.

## Equal in Extremes, Equal in Gold and Clod
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 6.7–6.9

For the self-conquered, the peaceful, the supreme Self is collected in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, and likewise in honor and dishonor. The one satisfied in knowledge and realization, standing on the peak, senses conquered — that yogin is called integrated, to whom clod, stone, and gold are equal. Surpassing is the one of equal understanding toward well-wishers, friends, enemies, neutrals, mediators, the hateful, and kin — and toward the good and the evil as well.

---

### Devanagari

जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः।

शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः

ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः।

युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः

सुहृन्मित्रार्युदासीनमध्यस्थद्वेष्यबन्धुषु।

साधुष्वपि च पापेषु समबुद्धिर्विशिष्यते

### IAST

jitātmanaḥ praśāntasya paramātmā samāhitaḥ|

śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu tathā mānāpamānayoḥ

jñānavijñānatṛptātmā kūṭastho vijitendriyaḥ|

yukta ityucyate yogī samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ

suhṛnmitrāryudāsīnamadhyasthadveṣyabandhuṣu|

sādhuṣvapi ca pāpeṣu samabuddhirviśiṣyate

### Pratibha Translation

For the self-conquered, the peaceful, the supreme Self is gathered in cold-heat, pleasure-pain, and honor-dishonor. Satisfied in knowledge and realization, peak-steady, senses conquered — that yogin is called integrated, to whom clod, stone, and gold are the same. Distinguished is the one of equal understanding toward ally, friend, enemy, neutral, mediator, the hateful, and kin — and toward the good and the sinful alike.

### Pratibha Commentary

Paramātman is samāhita for the jita and praśānta across climatic, hedonic, and status pairs. Yukta is further marked by jñāna-vijñāna satisfaction, kūṭastha steadiness, conquered senses, and value-equality of loṣṭa-aśma-kāñcana. Then the social summit: samabuddhi across the full relational spectrum, including sādhu and pāpa. The contested claim is that integration is tested not in cave silence but in honor’s volatility and in human ambivalence. Existentially, gold vs clod and friend vs foe are the exams. If your buddhi still surges with status and faction, the supreme Self is not yet collected in you. Equality across climate, pleasure, status, substances, and social factions is the phenomenological proof that Paramātman is collected and the yogin yoked. Gold-versus-clod and friend-versus-foe are not optional advanced tests; they are where kūṭastha steadiness shows. Samabuddhi that includes the sinner prevents holiness from becoming factional anesthesia. If honor and hatred still swing your buddhi, integration remains incomplete. Let extremes examine you.

### Key Terms

**kūṭastha (कूटस्थ)** — standing on the peak/immovable -> steadiness beyond fluctuation -> mountain-peak metaphor for consciousness

**samaloṣṭāśmakāñcana (समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चन)** — equal toward clod, stone, gold -> value-equality of substances -> dismantles greed’s ontology

**samabuddhi (समबुद्धि)** — equal understanding -> impartial cognition across persons -> ethical flower of yoga equality

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Marcus Aurelius on indifferent materials and difficult people:** Structural homology in equal mind across status goods and social types.
*Divergence:* Stoic cosmopolitanism differs from Gītā kūṭastha-paramātman collection language.

**Mengzi / Confucian impartial care debates:** Structural homology in extending regard beyond faction.
*Divergence:* Confucian graded love often remains; the Gītā’s samabuddhi explicitly includes enemy and sinner in equal understanding.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

Hold equal mind for ten minutes toward a valued object and a trivial one, then toward a liked and disliked person, without forcing fake affection — only refusing buddhi’s wild upgrade/downgrade.

## Alone, on a Clean Seat, for Self-Purification
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 6.10–6.12

Let the yogin yoke the self continually, staying in solitude, alone, mind and self restrained, without longing, without grasping. Establishing for oneself a firm seat in a clean place — not too high, not too low — with cloth, skin, and kuśa layered. There, making the mind one-pointed, with thought and sense-activity restrained, sitting on the seat, one should practice yoga for purification of the self.

---

### Devanagari

योगी युञ्जीत सततमात्मानं रहसि स्थितः।

एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा निराशीरपरिग्रहः

शुचौ देशे प्रतिष्ठाप्य स्थिरमासनमात्मनः।

नात्युच्छ्रितं नातिनीचं चैलाजिनकुशोत्तरम्

तत्रैकाग्रं मनः कृत्वा यतचित्तेन्द्रियक्रियः।

उपविश्यासने युञ्ज्याद्योगमात्मविशुद्धये

### IAST

yogī yuñjīta satatamātmānaṃ rahasi sthitaḥ|

ekākī yatacittātmā nirāśīraparigrahaḥ

śucau deśe pratiṣṭhāpya sthiramāsanamātmanaḥ|

nātyucchritaṃ nātinīcaṃ cailājinakuśottaram

tatraikāgraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā yatacittendriyakriyaḥ|

upaviśyāsane yuñjyādyogamātmaviśuddhaye

### Pratibha Translation

Let the yogin continually yoke the self, staying in secret, alone, with mind-self restrained, without longing and without grasping. Having established a firm seat for oneself in a clean place — not too high, not too low — covered with cloth, skin, and kuśa. There, making the mind one-pointed, restraining the activities of mind and senses, sitting on the seat, one should practice yoga for purification of the self.

### Pratibha Commentary

Meditation here is infrastructural before it is mystical: solitude, aloneness, restrained citta-ātman, nirāśī, aparigraha; then a śuci place, stable āsana of measured height, layered seat; then ekāgra mind and yoked practice for ātma-viśuddhi. The contested claim is that purification is the explicit aim of seating — not experience-collecting. In classical yoga this is the Gītā’s near-manual moment. Existentially, stop blaming “lack of insight” when seat, place, and longing still sabotage. Build the conditions. Continual yoking (satatam) matters more than occasional peak states. Infrastructure before mystique: solitude, non-grasping, clean mid-height seat, one-pointed mind, purification aim. Continual yoking matters more than occasional fireworks. If longing and clutter still set the room’s weather, insight claims will keep collapsing. Build conditions that make return possible. Dedicate sitting to ātma-viśuddhi so experience-collecting cannot hijack the session. The contested force of the passage remains practical: it asks for a change in how you inhabit action, attention, and relation — not for ornamental agreement. Return to the line until the claim bites a live decision today.

### Key Terms

**ekāgra (एकाग्र)** — one-pointed -> mind made single-tipped -> technical condition of practice on the seat

**aparigraha (अपरिग्रह)** — non-grasping -> outer condition of the yogin’s solitude -> links meditation to non-possessiveness

**ātmaiviśuddhi (आत्मविशुद्धि)** — purification of the self -> purpose of yuñjīta yoga -> teleology of the seating instructions

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Desert monastic cell discipline:** Structural homology in solitude, measured place, and purification aim.
*Divergence:* Monastic cell is christological-ascetic; here the seat-layers and ekāgra mind serve yogic ātma-viśuddhi.

**Patañjali’s āsana-sthira-sukha lineage:** Structural homology in stable seating as base for interior work.
*Divergence:* Patañjali systematizes eight limbs; the Gītā compresses a practical vignette within dhyāna-yoga teaching.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

Prepare a clean, mid-height seat; sit alone without phone for fifteen minutes, aim mind to one point, and dedicate the sitting solely to purification rather than to results.

## Body Aligned, Mind on Me
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 6.13–6.15

Holding body, head, and neck aligned, motionless and steady, gazing at the tip of one’s nose without looking around — with peaceful self, fear gone, established in the vow of brahmacarya, mind restrained, thought on me, integrated, let one sit devoted to me as highest. Yoking the self thus always, the yogin of controlled mind attains peace that is the supreme nirvāṇa, established in me.

---

### Devanagari

समं कायशिरोग्रीवं धारयन्नचलं स्थिरः।

संप्रेक्ष्य नासिकाग्रं स्वं दिशश्चानवलोकयन्

प्रशान्तात्मा विगतभीर्ब्रह्मचारिव्रते स्थितः।

मनः संयम्य मच्चित्तो युक्त आसीत मत्परः

युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी नियतमानसः।

शान्तिं निर्वाणपरमां मत्संस्थामधिगच्छति

### IAST

samaṃ kāyaśirogrīvaṃ dhārayannacalaṃ sthiraḥ|

saṃprekṣya nāsikāgraṃ svaṃ diśaścānavalokayan

praśāntātmā vigatabhīrbrahmacārivrate sthitaḥ|

manaḥ saṃyamya maccitto yukta āsīta matparaḥ

yuñjannevaṃ sadā''tmānaṃ yogī niyatamānasaḥ|

śāntiṃ nirvāṇaparamāṃ matsaṃsthāmadhigacchati

### Pratibha Translation

Holding body, head, and neck even, unmoving and firm, gazing at the tip of one’s own nose, not looking about in the directions — peaceful in self, fear gone, established in the brahmacarya vow, restraining the mind, with thought on me, integrated, let one sit having me as supreme. Yoking the self always in this way, the yogin of controlled mind reaches the peace that is supreme nirvāṇa, abiding in me.

### Pratibha Commentary

Posture precision joins theistic devotion: aligned kāya-śiras-grīvā, nose-tip gaze, no looking around; then praśānta, fearless, brahmacarya-vrata, mind restrained, mac-citta, mat-para. The contested synthesis is that dhyāna’s body mechanics culminate in mat-saṃsthā peace — nirvāṇa-paramā as abiding in Krishna. Technique without devotion is incomplete here; devotion without bodily steadiness is also incomplete. Existentially, let the spine teach the mind, and let the mind’s content be the Lord rather than self-monitoring vanity. Continual yoking yields peace that is not mood but establishment. Aligned body and nose-tip gaze are not ends; they serve mac-citta and mat-para sitting that ripens into peace as abiding in the Lord. Fearlessness and brahmacarya support the same theistic concentration. Technique without devotion and devotion without steadiness both fail this vignette. Let the spine teach, and let mind’s content be the Lord rather than self-surveillance. Continual yoking yields establishment, not a mood trophy. The contested force of the passage remains practical: it asks for a change in how you inhabit action, attention, and relation — not for ornamental agreement. Return to the line until the claim bites a live decision today.

### Key Terms

**maccitta (मच्चित्त)** — mind on me / thought formed of me -> theistic content of meditation -> specifies what ekāgratā is for

**matsaṃsthā (मत्संस्था)** — abiding/establishment in me -> the locus of supreme nirvāṇa-peace -> personalist seal on meditative attainment

**brahmacārivrata (ब्रह्मचारिव्रत)** — vow of brahmacarya -> disciplined sexual/energetic continence supporting sitting -> ethical base of dhyāna

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Hesychast posture and Name:** Structural homology in bodily alignment joined to personal divine focus.
*Divergence:* Jesus Prayer theology differs from Krishna-matpara establishment; both refuse posture-without-presence.

**Sufi murāqaba with beloved focus:** Structural homology in watchfulness ordered toward a personal Absolute.
*Divergence:* Sufi love-idiom and silsila differ; Gītā specifies nose-gaze and brahmacarya-vrata in epic yoga idiom.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

Sit aligned and still; rest gaze toward the nose tip without strain; when mind wanders, return it as “on You,” and end by sensing peace as abiding rather than as achievement.

## Yoga Fails Extremes of Food and Sleep
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 6.16

Yoga is not for one who eats too much or who does not eat at all, nor for one who sleeps too much or who stays forever awake, Arjuna.

---

### Devanagari

नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः।

न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन

### IAST

nātyaśnatastu yogo'sti na caikāntamanaśnataḥ|

na cātisvapnaśīlasya jāgrato naiva cārjuna

### Pratibha Translation

Yoga is not for the overeater, nor for one who entirely refrains from eating, nor for one excessively given to sleep, nor for the one who stays awake without measure, Arjuna.

### Pratibha Commentary

Yoga is incompatible with extremity in the basic biological rhythms of eating and sleeping. The contested claim attacks both indulgence and showy deprivation: atyaśnata and ekāntam anaśnata alike miss yoga; so do oversleep and compulsive vigil. In classical discipline this is madhyama as physiological wisdom, not mediocrity. Existentially, check whether your “spiritual intensity” is actually dysregulated appetite or sleep. The path that ignores the organism’s measure will not yield the mind’s measure. Extremes of eating and sleeping sabotage yoga whether they look like indulgence or like heroic deprivation. The organism’s measure is part of the path’s intelligence. Dysregulated appetite or vigil often masquerades as spiritual intensity while making citta untrainable. Restore measure before blaming the teaching. Yoga is incompatible with a life that refuses biological sanity. The contested force of the passage remains practical: it asks for a change in how you inhabit action, attention, and relation — not for ornamental agreement. Return to the line until the claim bites a live decision today.

### Key Terms

**atyaśnata (अत्यश्नत्)** — overeating one -> extremity that blocks yoga -> body excess as spiritual obstacle

**ekāntam anaśnataḥ (एकान्तमनश्नत्)** — entirely not eating -> opposite extremity also blocking -> austerity theater without yoga

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Aristotle’s mean in bodily habits:** Structural homology in virtue as measured middle against twin vices.
*Divergence:* Aristotelian ethics aims at eudaimonia in the polis; here measure is specifically condition for yoga.

**Buddha’s Middle Way after extreme asceticism:** Structural homology in rejecting starvation vigil as awakening’s method.
*Divergence:* Buddhist Middle Way is path to nibbāna; the Gītā frames measure as prerequisite of dhyāna-yoga.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

For one day, keep food and sleep within a pre-set moderate window; refuse both binge and heroic skip as “for yoga.”

## Measured Living Makes Yoga the Killer of Pain
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 6.17

For one measured in food and recreation, measured in effort in actions, measured in sleep and waking — yoga becomes the destroyer of pain.

---

### Devanagari

युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु।

युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा

### IAST

yuktāhāravihārasya yuktaceṣṭasya karmasu|

yuktasvapnāvabodhasya yogo bhavati duḥkhahā

### Pratibha Translation

For one of measured food and recreation, measured in exertion in actions, measured in sleep and waking — yoga becomes the destroyer of pain.

### Pratibha Commentary

Yukta — measured/appropriate — applies to āhāra, vihāra, ceṣṭā in karma, and svapna-avabodha. Under that fourfold measure, yoga becomes duḥkha-hā. The contested claim is causal: meditation destroys pain when life’s tempos are already yoked. Without that, sitting often amplifies strain. In Gītā yoga hygiene, lifestyle is not “prep” beneath the real thing; it is part of the mechanism. Existentially, if practice increases misery, inspect measure before abandoning the path. Pain-killing yoga is a whole-life tuning. Fourfold yukta living — food, recreation, effort, sleep-waking — is not “prep” beneath real yoga; it is how yoga becomes pain’s destroyer. Unmeasured life turns sitting into amplified strain. If practice increases misery, inspect lifestyle tuning before abandoning the path. Pain-killing yoga is whole-life rhythm. Measure is mercy to the mind you hope to still. The contested force of the passage remains practical: it asks for a change in how you inhabit action, attention, and relation — not for ornamental agreement. Return to the line until the claim bites a live decision today.

### Key Terms

**yukta (युक्त)** — measured/yoked/appropriate -> the adjective of sustainable practice life -> against both chaos and rigidity theater

**duḥkhahā (दुःखहा)** — destroyer of pain -> yoga’s fruit under measure -> promises relief without promising anesthesia of denial

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Ayurvedic / dinacaryā wisdom:** Structural homology in rhythmic living as condition of mental clarity.
*Divergence:* Ayurveda centers doṣa balance; the Gītā ties measure explicitly to yoga as duḥkha-hā.

**Benedictine moderation (RB):** Structural homology in measured food, work, and rest for prayer’s sake.
*Divergence:* Benedictine measure serves liturgical community in Christ; here measure serves yogic destruction of duḥkha.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

Set measures for today’s eating, break, work effort, and sleep; practice a short yoga sit inside that measured day and notice pain’s edge blunt.

## Mind Stilled Like a Lamp in Windless Place
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 6.18–6.20

When the well-restrained mind stays in the Self alone, free from longing for all desires — then one is called integrated. As a lamp in a windless place does not flicker — that simile is recalled for the yogin of restrained mind practicing yoga of the self. When the mind, restrained by yoga practice, comes to rest, and when seeing the Self by the Self, one is content in the Self—

---

### Devanagari

यदा विनियतं चित्तमात्मन्येवावतिष्ठते।

निःस्पृहः सर्वकामेभ्यो युक्त इत्युच्यते तदा

यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता।

योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः

यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया।

यत्र चैवात्मनाऽऽत्मानं पश्यन्नात्मनि तुष्यति

### IAST

yadā viniyataṃ cittamātmanyevāvatiṣṭhate|

niḥspṛhaḥ sarvakāmebhyo yukta ityucyate tadā

yathā dīpo nivātastho neṅgate sopamā smṛtā|

yogino yatacittasya yuñjato yogamātmanaḥ

yatroparamate cittaṃ niruddhaṃ yogasevayā|

yatra caivātmanā''tmānaṃ paśyannātmani tuṣyati

### Pratibha Translation

When the well-disciplined mind abides in the Self alone, without longing for any desires — then one is called integrated. As a lamp standing in a windless place does not flicker — that comparison is remembered for the yogin of restrained mind practicing the yoga of the self. Where the mind comes to rest, restrained by yoga practice, and where seeing the Self by the Self one is content in the Self—

### Pratibha Commentary

Yukta is timed to a when: viniyata citta abides in ātman, niḥspṛha toward all kāmas. The lamp-in-nivāta image gives the phenomenology — non-flicker under restraint while practicing ātman’s yoga. Then the where: citta uparamate, niruddha by yoga-sevā; and Self is seen by Self with contentment in Self. The contested claim is that contentment is cognitive-visionary, not reward for concentration. In Pātañjala resonance, nirodha language appears inside Gītā bhakti-yoga framing. Existentially, stop calling every quiet mood “yoga.” Look for non-flicker, desirelessness, and Self-seeing contentment. That is the lamp. The lamp simile gives a criterion against drowsy dullness and forced blankness alike: non-flicker under restraint while practicing Self-yoga. Rest and Self-seeing contentment mark the where of integration, with desirelessness as climate. Quiet moods are not automatically this. Serve yoga repeatedly until flicker yields to lamp-steadiness and contentment in Self-seeing. That phenomenology is the teaching’s proof. The contested force of the passage remains practical: it asks for a change in how you inhabit action, attention, and relation — not for ornamental agreement. Return to the line until the claim bites a live decision today.

### Key Terms

**nivātastha dīpa (निवातस्थ दीप)** — lamp in windless place -> classic simile of unwavering citta -> stillness as non-oscillation

**yoga-sevā (योगसेवा)** — practice/service of yoga -> what restrains the mind to rest -> emphasizes repeated tending

**ātmanā ātmānam (आत्मना आत्मानम्)** — Self by the Self -> reflexive seeing -> knowing as self-revelation, not object hunt

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Patañjali YS 1.2–1.3:** Structural homology in restraint of citta and abiding in seer’s nature.
*Divergence:* Patañjali’s system is kleśa-oriented sūtra method; Gītā embeds nirodha-like rest in theistic dhyāna chapter.

**Plotinus on the soul’s stillness before the One:** Structural homology in non-flickering interior for vision.
*Divergence:* Plotinian vision ascends emanation hierarchy; here contentment is Self-seeing in ātman via yoga-sevā.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

Sit until you can feel the difference between drowsy dullness and lamp-like non-flicker; when flicker returns, gently re-serve yoga rather than forcing blankness.

## Infinite Happiness Beyond the Senses
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 6.21–6.23

That infinite happiness, to be grasped by understanding, beyond the senses — knowing it, established, one does not deviate from truth. Having gained which, one thinks no other gain greater; established in which, one is not shaken even by heavy sorrow. Let that be known as the disentangling from contact with pain — that is called yoga. That yoga must be practiced with determination, with undespairing mind.

---

### Devanagari

सुखमात्यन्तिकं यत्तद्बुद्धिग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम्।

वेत्ति यत्र न चैवायं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः

यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः।

यस्मिन्स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणापि विचाल्यते

तं विद्याद् दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम्।

स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा

### IAST

sukhamātyantikaṃ yattadbuddhigrāhyamatīndriyam|

vetti yatra na caivāyaṃ sthitaścalati tattvataḥ

yaṃ labdhvā cāparaṃ lābhaṃ manyate nādhikaṃ tataḥ|

yasminsthito na duḥkhena guruṇāpi vicālyate

taṃ vidyād duḥkhasaṃyogaviyogaṃ yogasaṃjñitam|

sa niścayena yoktavyo yogo'nirviṇṇacetasā

### Pratibha Translation

That ultimate happiness, graspable by understanding, beyond the senses — where one knows it and, established, does not waver from the real. Having gained which, one thinks no other gain greater; established in which, one is not moved even by heavy sorrow. Know that as the disjunction from conjunction with pain — named yoga. That yoga must be practiced with determination, with a mind that does not despair.

### Pratibha Commentary

Yoga is defined as duḥkha-saṃyoga-viyoga — disentangling from pain’s conjunction — and identified with ātyantika sukha that is buddhi-grāhya and atīndriya. The contested marks are stability in tattva, unsurpassable gain-evaluation, and unshakeability even under guru duḥkha. Then the method seal: practice with niścaya and anirviṇṇa-cetas — determined, non-despairing mind. In soteriological psychology this blocks both sensory happiness chasing and fragile enthusiasm. Existentially, if heavy sorrow still defines you absolutely, you have not yet stood in that yoga; if despair ends practice, you have mistaken intensity for determination. Keep yoking without theatrical hope or theatrical quit. Yoga as disentangling from pain-conjunction is also ultimate happiness known by buddhi beyond senses — positive and negative faces of one attainment. Unshakeability under heavy sorrow and refusal of greater-gain thinking are marks, not slogans. Practice then requires determination with undespairing mind, blocking both fragile enthusiasm and bitter quit. Keep yoking when sorrow is heavy. The definition stands only where standing does not waver.

### Key Terms

**ātyantika sukha (आत्यन्तिक सुख)** — ultimate/endless happiness -> buddhi-known, sense-transcending -> the positive face of yoga’s definition

**duḥkhasaṃyogaviyoga (दुःखसंयोगवियोग)** — disjunction from pain-conjunction -> technical definition of yoga here -> yoga as unbinding from suffering’s grip

**anirviṇṇacetas (अनिर्विण्णचेतस्)** — undespairing mind -> affective condition of practice -> endurance without bitterness

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Buddha’s Third Noble Truth:** Structural homology in defining the goal as cessation/disjunction from suffering’s link.
*Divergence:* Buddhist nirodha is framed without ātman-sukha doctrine; here yoga is also ultimate happiness known by buddhi.

**Boethius on happiness unshaken by fortune:** Structural homology in a good not surpassed and not overthrown by sorrow.
*Divergence:* Boethius’ Consolation is philosophical-theistic in a Roman key; the Gītā commands determined yogic practice toward that standing.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

When practice feels fruitless, renew determination without despair for one more measured sit; afterward, ask whether any quieter buddhi-happiness appeared beyond sense reward.

## Slowly, Slowly, Think Nothing
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 6.24–6.25

Abandoning without remainder all desires born of intention, restraining the sense-flock on every side by the mind alone — little by little let one come to rest by understanding held with firmness; making the mind abide in the Self, let one not think of anything at all.

---

### Devanagari

सङ्कल्पप्रभवान्कामांस्त्यक्त्वा सर्वानशेषतः।

मनसैवेन्द्रियग्रामं विनियम्य समन्ततः

शनैः शनैरुपरमेद् बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया।

आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत्

### IAST

saṅkalpaprabhavānkāmāṃstyaktvā sarvānaśeṣataḥ|

manasaivendriyagrāmaṃ viniyamya samantataḥ

śanaiḥ śanairuparamed buddhyā dhṛtigṛhītayā|

ātmasaṃsthaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā na kiñcidapi cintayet

### Pratibha Translation

Abandoning without remainder all desires born of intention, restraining the flock of senses on every side by the mind alone — slowly, slowly let one come to rest by understanding gripped with firmness; making the mind established in the Self, let one not think of anything whatsoever.

### Pratibha Commentary

The method is ordered: total tyāga of saṅkalpa-born kāmas; mental restraint of the indriya-grāma on all sides; then śanaiḥ śanaiḥ uparama with buddhi held by dhṛti; mind made ātma-saṃstha; finally na kiñcid api cintayet. The contested pace — slowly, slowly — refuses violent blanking. Firmness (dhṛti) holds buddhi while rest arrives gradually. In meditation pedagogy this is gold: ending thought is the fruit of establishment, not the first forced act. Existentially, if you try to think nothing while desires still author the mind, you only breed underground saṅkalpa. Drop desire-seeds, herd the senses, settle slowly, then let thinking thin. Gradualism is doctrinal: slowly, slowly come to rest with firm-held buddhi after desires born of intention are abandoned and senses herded by mind. Thinking nothing is culmination after Self-establishment, not the first violent act. Forced blanking while saṅkalpa still authors the mind breeds underground wanting. Drop seeds, restrain the flock, settle gradually, then let thought thin. Firmness holds the process without haste.

### Key Terms

**śanaiḥ śanaiḥ (शनैः शनैः)** — slowly, slowly -> mandatory gradualism of resting -> against abrupt suppression fantasies

**dhṛtigṛhītā buddhi (धृतिगृहीता बुद्धि)** — understanding held by firmness -> the grip that allows gradual rest -> steadiness as method

**na kiñcid api cintayet (न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत्)** — should not think anything at all -> culmination after Self-establishment -> not first technique

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Cloud of Unknowing’s gradual work:** Structural homology in releasing discursive thought toward simple resting in God/Self.
*Divergence:* Cloud is apophatic Christian; Gītā specifies saṅkalpa-desire abandonment and sense-herding first.

**Dzogchen / Mahāmudrā gradual vs sudden debates:** Structural homology in tension between slow settling and non-thinking.
*Divergence:* Those systems have distinct view-practices; here gradual uparama is explicit scriptural method.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

Drop one intention-born desire, restrain senses with mind for a few minutes, then settle “slowly, slowly” into Self-abiding until thoughts thin — without attacking thoughts as enemies.

## Wherever the Mind Runs, Bring It Back
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 6.26

Wherever the restless, unsteady mind goes out, from there restrain it and bring it under control in the Self alone.

---

### Devanagari

यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम्।

ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत्

### IAST

yato yato niścarati manaścañcalamasthiram|

tatastato niyamyaitadātmanyeva vaśaṃ nayet

### Pratibha Translation

Wherever, wherever the restless, unsteady mind goes forth — from there, from there restrain it and lead it to control in the Self alone.

### Pratibha Commentary

The verse assumes wandering rather than forbidding it by fantasy. Yato yato … tatas tataḥ: each exit is a handle for return. The contested gentleness-within-firmness is that cañcala-asthira mind is trained by repeated niyama and vaśa-nayana into ātman, not by one annihilating stroke. In practical dhyāna this is the basic loop of yoga. Existentially, shame at distraction is mostly ego; the work is return. Every outgoing is usable. Bring it back to Self-control again. Wandering is assumed; each outgoing is a handle. Shame at distraction mostly serves ego, while the work is return — restrain and lead into Self-control again and again. This loop is dhyāna’s ordinary holiness. Success is counted in returns, not in unbroken fantasy stillness. Bring it back from wherever it went; the map is made of those wherevers. The contested force of the passage remains practical: it asks for a change in how you inhabit action, attention, and relation — not for ornamental agreement. Return to the line until the claim bites a live decision today.

### Key Terms

**cañcala (चञ्चल)** — restless/flickering -> mind’s native mobility -> normalized as the field of training

**vaśaṃ nayet (वशं नयेत्)** — should lead to control -> active shepherding into ātman -> agency in the return

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Patañjali’s abhyāsa definition (YS 1.13–14):** Structural homology in repeated practice stabilizing wandering citta.
*Divergence:* Patañjali pairs abhyāsa with vairāgya systematically; this verse isolates the return loop to ātman.

**Christian monologistic prayer / returning to the word:** Structural homology in non-dramatic return from distraction.
*Divergence:* Return is to a prayer-word/Name; here return is into ātman’s control.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

In sitting, each time mind leaves, mark “there,” restrain without insult, and lead attention into Self — count twenty returns as success, not failure.

## Quiet Rajas, Brahman-Touch Happiness
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 6.27–6.28

Supreme happiness comes to this yogin whose mind is peaceful, whose rajas is stilled, who has become Brahman, stainless. Yoking the self always thus, the yogin freed from stain easily enjoys the infinite happiness of contact with Brahman.

---

### Devanagari

उपैति शान्तरजसं ब्रह्मभूतमकल्मषम्

युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी विगतकल्मषः।

सुखेन ब्रह्मसंस्पर्शमत्यन्तं सुखमश्नुते

### IAST

### Pratibha Translation

Supreme happiness comes to this yogin of peaceful mind, whose rajas is quieted, who has become Brahman, without stain. Yoking the self always in this way, the yogin whose stain is gone easily enjoys the infinite happiness of Brahman-contact.

### Pratibha Commentary

Uttama sukha approaches the yogin who is praśānta-manas, śānta-rajas, brahma-bhūta, akalmaṣa. Continual yoking then yields easy enjoyment of brahma-saṃsparśa’s atyanta sukha. The contested physiology-metaphysics is rajas quieting as condition of Brahman-becoming happiness — not as depression, but as cooling of agitated passion-quality. Existentially, if happiness feels forced, check whether rajas is still driving the sit. Ease (sukhena) is itself a sign: stain-gone contact is not gritted teeth. Become cool enough for contact to be joy. Quieted rajas is cooled agitation, not depressive collapse — the guṇa climate in which Brahman-becoming happiness can approach. Easy enjoyment of Brahman-contact signals stain-gone practice; gritted bliss is usually still rajas in costume. Continual yoking makes contact joyful rather than forced. Cool the drivers of speed and heat, then look for happiness that arrives as ease. Supreme sukha approaches a peaceful, stainless, Brahman-become mind. The contested force of the passage remains practical: it asks for a change in how you inhabit action, attention, and relation — not for ornamental agreement. Return to the line until the claim bites a live decision today.

### Key Terms

**śāntarajas (शान्तरजस्)** — whose rajas is quieted -> guṇa-level description of meditative readiness -> links happiness to cosmic psychology

**brahmasaṃsparśa (ब्रह्मसंस्पर्श)** — contact/touch of Brahman -> intimate metaphor for realization’s joy -> not spatial touch; contact-as-knowing

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Guṇa theory elsewhere in Gītā (chs. 14, 18):** Structural homology in rajas as agitation opposing clarity and peace.
*Divergence:* Later chapters systematize three guṇas; here quieted rajas is specifically tied to brahma-bhūta happiness.

**Apophatic “touch” of God (e.g., Ruusbroec):** Structural homology in contact-language for non-sensory union joy.
*Divergence:* Christian mystical touch is trinitarian; here brahma-saṃsparśa follows rajas-stilling yoga.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

Before sitting, cool one rajas trigger (speed, argument, caffeine spike); then yoke and look for happiness that arrives as ease of contact, not as hype.

## Self in All Beings, All Beings in Self
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 6.29

Whose self is yoked in yoga sees the Self abiding in all beings and all beings in the Self — same-seeing everywhere.

---

### Devanagari

सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि।

ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः

### IAST

sarvabhūtasthamātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani|

### Pratibha Translation

The yoga-yoked self sees the Self standing in all beings and all beings in the Self — same-seeing everywhere.

### Pratibha Commentary

Vision becomes double and reciprocal: ātman in all bhūtas, all bhūtas in ātman, with sarvatra samadarśana. The contested claim is that yoga-yoking produces a seeing, not only a private calm. In Upaniṣadic-Gītā non-dual ethics, this is the perceptual basis of compassion without condescension. Existentially, test your practice in the street. If calm collapses into ranking beings, yoking has not yet opened seeing. Same-seeing everywhere is the fruit that proves the sit. Yoga-yoking must produce seeing: Self in beings, beings in Self, same-seeing everywhere. Private calm that fails in the street is incomplete. This reciprocal vision is the perceptual basis of compassion without condescension. Test practice among bodies that trigger ranking. If samadarśana collapses, return to yoking until vision holds. The contested force of the passage remains practical: it asks for a change in how you inhabit action, attention, and relation — not for ornamental agreement. Return to the line until the claim bites a live decision today.

### Key Terms

**sarvabhūtastha (सर्वभूतस्थ)** — standing in all beings -> Self’s omnipresence as seen -> vision-claim, not slogan

**samadarśana (समदर्शन)** — same-seeing -> equality of vision everywhere -> ethical phenomenology of yoga

### Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Īśā Upaniṣad 6–7:** Structural homology in seeing all in the Self and Self in all.
*Divergence:* Īśā’s compact mantra differs in tone; Gītā ties the vision explicitly to yogayuktātman practice.

**Franciscan / creation-seeing traditions:** Structural homology in finding the sacred across creatures.
*Divergence:* Franciscan seeing is christocentric praise; here reciprocal Self-beings vision is yogic-samadarśana.

### Practice (Abhyasa)

After sitting, walk among people and silently see Self-in-them and them-in-Self once each, without preaching the vision.

## Who Sees Me Everywhere Does Not Lose Me
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 6.30–6.31

Who sees me everywhere and sees all in me — I am not lost to that one, nor is that one lost to me. Who worships me as abiding in all beings, established in oneness — that yogin dwells in me, however they may live.

---

### Devanagari

यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति।

तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति

सर्वभूतस्थितं यो मां भजत्येकत्वमास्थितः।

सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्तते

### IAST

yo māṃ paśyati sarvatra sarvaṃ ca mayi paśyati|
