## A Single Fragment Upholds the World
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 10.42

But what is this extensive knowledge to you, O Arjuna? I support this whole universe with a single portion of Myself.

---

### Devanagari
अथवा बहुनैतेन किं ज्ञातेन तवार्जुन।

विष्टभ्याहमिदं कृत्स्नमेकांशेन स्थितो जगत्

### IAST
athavā bahunaitena kiṃ jñātena tavārjuna|

viṣṭabhyāhamidaṃ kṛtsnamekāṃśena sthito jagat

### Pratibha Translation
But what is this extensive knowledge to you, O Arjuna? I support this whole universe with a single portion of Myself.

### Pratibha Commentary
The chapter ends by undercutting its own catalog: what need of this vistara? The universe stands on ekena aṃśena — one fragment of Me. The contested climax is simultaneous generosity and reserve: endless vibhūtis were nectar, yet all worlds are held by a portion. Existentially this births awe without exhaustion and devotion without mastery-compulsion. You have been shown peaks; now learn that the whole show is fraction. Rest in that disproportion. The teaching's force is practical: what it claims about reality must reshape attention and choice, or it remains ornamental. If rehearsal does not change in ordinary time, the claim will not hold when pressure rises. The teaching's force is practical: what it claims about reality must reshape attention and choice, or it remains ornamental. If rehearsal does not change in ordinary time, the claim will not hold when pressure rises. Live one concrete implication of the claim before the day ends, so the argument becomes conduct rather than ornament.

### Key Terms
**aṃśa (अंश)** — portion -> the single portion supporting the universe -> "part" as spatial piece understates power-disproportion
**vistara (विस्तर)** — extension/detail -> the extensive knowing Arjuna is told he does not finally need -> "long lecture" misses revelatory expanse now relativized

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Job's final humility after theophany]:** Shared move from expansive disclosure to human-size awe.
*Divergence:* Job is silenced; Arjuna is prepared for the vision of chapter 11.
**[Dao De Jing 4/6 on inexhaustible use]:** Shared sense of source not depleted by world-support.
*Divergence:* Daoist emptiness idiom vs Gītā's personal ekena aṃśena.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
After any long study session, close with: "the universe hangs on a portion — I do not need to finish owning the map." Bow once and stop.

## From Hearing to Wanting Vision
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 11.1–11.3

Arjuna said: By the supreme secret concerning the self, spoken in Your grace, this delusion of mine has gone. The arising and passing of beings I have heard from You in detail, O Lotus-eyed, and also Your imperishable majesty. Just as You have described Yourself, O Supreme Lord, I wish to see Your lordly form, O Highest Person.

---

### Devanagari
अर्जुन उवाच

मदनुग्रहाय परमं गुह्यमध्यात्मसंज्ञितम्।

यत्त्वयोक्तं वचस्तेन मोहोऽयं विगतो मम

भवाप्ययौ हि भूतानां श्रुतौ विस्तरशो मया।

त्वत्तः कमलपत्राक्ष माहात्म्यमपि चाव्ययम्

एवमेतद्यथात्थ त्वमात्मानं परमेश्वर।

द्रष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपमैश्वरं पुरुषोत्तम

### IAST
arjuna uvāca

madanugrahāya paramaṃ guhyamadhyātmasaṃjñitam|

yattvayoktaṃ vacastena moho'yaṃ vigato mama

bhavāpyayau hi bhūtānāṃ śrutau vistaraśo mayā|

tvattaḥ kamalapatrākṣa māhātmyamapi cāvyayam

evametadyathāttha tvamātmānaṃ parameśvara|

draṣṭumicchāmi te rūpamaiśvaraṃ puruṣottama

### Pratibha Translation
Arjuna said: By the supreme secret concerning the self, spoken in Your grace, this delusion of mine has gone. The arising and passing of beings I have heard from You in detail, O Lotus-eyed, and also Your imperishable majesty. Just as You have described Yourself, O Supreme Lord, I wish to see Your lordly form, O Highest Person.

### Pratibha Commentary
Hearing has done real work: moha is gone. Yet Arjuna asks to see — not from disbelief but from the logic of grace-received secret. The contested move is that right hearing awakens desire for darshana of aishvara rupa. Existentially this validates hunger for vision without scorning the prior verbal teaching. Delusion's removal is not the end; it is clearance for a more dangerous seeing. Wanting to see the Lord as the Lord has described Himself is fidelity, not curiosity-as-entertainment. The teaching's force is practical: what it claims about reality must reshape attention and choice, or it remains ornamental. If rehearsal does not change in ordinary time, the claim will not hold when pressure rises. The teaching's force is practical: what it claims about reality must reshape attention and choice, or it remains ornamental. If rehearsal does not change in ordinary time, the claim will not hold when pressure rises. Live one concrete implication of the claim before the day ends, so the argument becomes conduct rather than ornament.

### Key Terms
**moha (मोह)** — delusion -> what Arjuna says has departed through gracious teaching -> 'confusion' understates bondage-character of moha
**aiśvara rūpa (ऐश्वर रूप)** — lordly form -> what Arjuna wants to see -> 'majestic appearance' misses sovereignty-form

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Thomas' desire to see (John 20)]:** Shared movement from word to wanting vision.
*Divergence:* Resurrection verification differs; Arjuna asks after moha already gone.
**[Moses asking to see glory (Exodus 33)]:** Shared request for divine self-showing after relationship.
*Divergence:* Biblical glory-limits differ; Gita will grant a cosmic form through divine eye.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
After study today, ask whether you want only more words or a truer seeing. Name the difference without forcing an experience.

## If You Think I Can See — Show Yourself
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 11.4–11.6

If You think it possible for me to see this, O Lord, then, O Master of Yoga, show me Your imperishable Self. The Blessed Lord said: Behold My forms, O Partha, by hundreds and thousands — various, divine, of various colors and shapes. Behold the Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, the two Ashvins, and the Maruts; behold many wonders not seen before, O Bharata.

---

### Devanagari

श्री भगवानुवाच

पश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः।

नानाविधानि दिव्यानि नानावर्णाकृतीनि च

पश्यादित्यान्वसून्रुद्रानश्िवनौ मरुतस्तथा।

बहून्यदृष्टपूर्वाणि पश्याऽश्चर्याणि भारत

### IAST
manyase yadi tacchakyaṃ mayā draṣṭumiti prabho|

śrī bhagavānuvāca

paśya me pārtha rūpāṇi śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ|

nānāvidhāni divyāni nānāvarṇākṛtīni ca

paśyādityānvasūnrudrānaśivanau marutastathā|

bahūnyadṛṣṭapūrvāṇi paśyā'ścaryāṇi bhārata

### Pratibha Translation
If You think it possible for me to see this, O Lord, then, O Master of Yoga, show me Your imperishable Self. The Blessed Lord said: Behold My forms, O Partha, by hundreds and thousands — various, divine, of various colors and shapes. Behold the Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, the two Ashvins, and the Maruts; behold many wonders not seen before, O Bharata.

### Pratibha Commentary
Vision is granted not seized, yet once granted it commands looking. The contested move in this stretch of the vision is that arjuna asks to be shown if able; krishna commands behold hundreds of divine forms and gods. Existentially the line forces a choice about how you relate to overwhelm, agency, and devotion after seeing. Do not aestheticize the theophany; let it revise what you think action, fear, and love are for. The chapter's pedagogy moves from granted seeing to ethical-devotional walking; this unit is one step on that arc. The teaching's force is practical: what it claims about reality must reshape attention and choice, or it remains ornamental. If rehearsal does not change in ordinary time, the claim will not hold when pressure rises. The teaching's force is practical: what it claims about reality must reshape attention and choice, or it remains ornamental. If rehearsal does not change in ordinary time, the claim will not hold when pressure rises. Live one concrete implication of the claim before the day ends, so the argument becomes conduct rather than ornament.

### Key Terms
**Yogeśvara (योगेश्वर)** — passage key term -> Vision is granted not seized, yet once granted it commands looking. -> default gloss flattens the vision's force
**paśya (पश्य)** — paired key term -> Arjuna asks to be shown if able; Krishna commands behold hundreds of divine forms and gods. -> soft translation misses structural role

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Eleusinian initiation]:** Structural kinship around granted vision under condition.
*Divergence:* Frame diverges from Gita 11's battlefield visvarupa pedagogy.
**[Islamic miraj]:** Shared pressure of granted vision under condition.
*Divergence:* Different metaphysics; Gita binds the moment to Krishna's first-person disclosure.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Practice one 'if You think I can' request before hard seeing, then actually look.

The teaching's force is practical: what it claims about reality must reshape attention and choice, or it remains ornamental. idānīmasmi saṃvṛttaḥ sacetāḥ prakṛtiṃ gataḥ

### Pratibha Translation
Do not tremble, do not be confused from seeing this fearsome form of Mine; free of fear, mind at peace, see again this very form of Mine. Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus, Vasudeva showed again His own form; the Great Self consoled the terrified, becoming again the gentle pleasant form. Arjuna said: Seeing this human form of Yours, gracious, O Janardana, I am now composed, mind restored.

### Pratibha Commentary
Fierce truth and gentle presence are one Self in modes; consolation is not denial. The contested move in this stretch of the vision is that do not tremble; see again this form; vasudeva shows gentle human form; arjuna composed again. Existentially the line forces a choice about how you relate to overwhelm, agency, and devotion after seeing. Do not aestheticize the theophany; let it revise what you think action, fear, and love are for. The chapter's pedagogy moves from granted seeing to ethical-devotional walking; this unit is one step on that arc. The teaching's force is practical: what it claims about reality must reshape attention and choice, or it remains ornamental. If rehearsal does not change in ordinary time, the claim will not hold when pressure rises. **saumya (सौम्य)** — passage key term -> Fierce truth and gentle presence are one Self in modes; consolation is not denial. -> default gloss flattens the vision's force
**mānuṣa (मानुष)** — paired key term -> Do not tremble; see again this form; Vasudeva shows gentle human form; Arjuna composed again. -> soft translation misses structural role

## Which Yoga Knows Best?
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 12.1–12.3

Arjuna said: Those devotees who, ever joined, worship You, and those who worship the imperishable unmanifest — which of them are the best knowers of yoga?

The Blessed Lord said: Those who fix the mind on Me, ever joined, worship Me, endowed with supreme faith — they are held by Me to be the most joined.

But those who worship the imperishable, the indefinable, the unmanifest, the all-pervading, unthinkable, the immovable, the constant—

---

### Devanagari
अर्जुन उवाचएवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्युपासते।येचाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं तेषां के योगवित्तमाः

श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते।श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः

ये त्वक्षरमनिर्देश्यमव्यक्तं पर्युपासते।सर्वत्रगमचिन्त्यं च कूटस्थमचलं ध्रुवम्

### IAST
arjuna uvācaevaṃ satatayuktā ye bhaktāstvāṃ paryupāsate|yecāpyakṣaramavyaktaṃ teṣāṃ ke yogavittamāḥ

śrī bhagavānuvācamayyāveśya mano ye māṃ nityayuktā upāsate|śraddhayā parayopetāste me yuktatamā matāḥ

ye tvakṣaramanirdeśyamavyaktaṃ paryupāsate|sarvatragamacintyaṃ ca kūṭasthamacalaṃ dhruvam

### Pratibha Translation
Arjuna said: Those devotees ever joined who worship You, and those who worship the imperishable unmanifest [akṣara avyakta] — which of them are the best knowers of yoga?

The Blessed Lord said: Those who enter the mind into Me, ever joined, worship Me, endowed with the highest faith [śraddhā] — they are held by Me to be the most yoked.

But those who worship the imperishable, indefinable, unmanifest, all-pervading, unthinkable, the peak-still [kūṭastha], unmoving, firm—

### Pratibha Commentary
Arjuna's question is comparative without being cynical: personal devotion versus unmanifest Absolute — who knows yoga best? Kṛṣṇa's contested answer ranks without annihilating the second path: those who fix mind on Me with supreme faith are yuktatama — most joined. The unmanifest worshippers are not dismissed; they are introduced with a "but" that will continue into difficulty and eventual arrival. Existentially this refuses both anti-intellectual bhakti-chauvinism and cool contempt for devotion. The criterion of "best" is not aesthetic preference; it is degree of joining under faith. Faith here is not soft belief but the supreme trust that allows mind to enter the Lord. The chapter will soon admit the unmanifest path reaches the same Me — at greater cost for the embodied. Ranking is pedagogical mercy: start where joining is most possible. The line-level force of the teaching is practical, not ornamental: what it claims about reality is meant to reshape how you attend, choose, and depart. If the claim does not alter rehearsal in ordinary time, it will not hold when time thins. Existential uptake is therefore part of fidelity to the argument, not an optional aftertaste.

### Key Terms
**yuktatama (युक्ततम)** — most yoked/joined -> Kṛṣṇa's evaluation of personal devotees with supreme faith -> "best yogi" as status contest misses joining-intensity.

**akṣara avyakta (अक्षरमव्यक्त)** — imperishable unmanifest -> the alternative worship-object in Arjuna's question -> "formless God" is approximate but loses technical pair with personal worship.

**śraddhā (श्रद्धा)** — faith/trust -> supreme faith qualifying the most joined -> "belief" as opinion is too thin.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**Cloud of Unknowing vs. affective devotion debates:** Both traditions argue relative excellence of apophatic vs personal love paths.
*Divergence:* Medieval Christian framing differs; Gītā ranks inside one Lord's first-person pedagogy.

**Plotinus' ascent vs theurgic devotion:** Structural tension between formless One and personal cult.
*Divergence:* Plotinus subordinates cult; Gītā elevates personal joining as yuktatama while still validating unmanifest worship.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Ask honestly which path you actually practice when tired: personal address, or abstract unmanifest. Practice that path today with supreme faith rather than hybrid vagueness.

## Harder Path, Same Arrival — Softened by Offering
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 12.4–12.6

— restraining the multitude of senses, equal-minded everywhere, rejoicing in the welfare of all beings — they also reach Me.

The difficulty is greater for those whose minds are attached to the unmanifest; for the unmanifest goal is reached with suffering by the embodied.

But those who renounce all actions in Me, intent on Me, meditating on Me with undivided yoga, worship Me—

---

### Devanagari
संनियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्वत्र समबुद्धयः।ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्वभूतहिते रताः

क्लेशोऽधिकतरस्तेषामव्यक्तासक्तचेतसाम्।

अव्यक्ता हि गतिर्दुःखं देहवद्भिरवाप्यते

ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः।अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते

### IAST
saṃniyamyendriyagrāmaṃ sarvatra samabuddhayaḥ|te prāpnuvanti māmeva sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ

kleśo'dhikatarasteṣāmavyaktāsaktacetasām|

avyaktā hi gatirduḥkhaṃ dehavadbhiravāpyate

ye tu sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya matparāḥ|ananyenaiva yogena māṃ dhyāyanta upāsate

### Pratibha Translation
Having restrained the sense-host, equal-minded everywhere, delighting in the good of all beings — they also reach Me alone.

Greater is the trouble for those whose awareness clings to the unmanifest; for the unmanifest path is reached painfully by the embodied.

But those who renounce all actions in Me, intent on Me as supreme, meditating on Me with undivided yoga, worship—

### Pratibha Commentary
The unmanifest path is affirmed: sense-restraint, sameness everywhere, dedication to all beings' welfare — and they reach Me. The contested pastoral claim follows: for the embodied, avyakta-attachment brings greater kleśa. Embodiment makes formless goal hard; this is anthropology, not insult. Then the alternative is named: renounce actions in Me, be mat-para, meditate with ananya yoga. Existentially this legitimizes needing form, relation, and offering without calling it inferior metaphysics. If you are embodied and find pure unmanifest practice grinding you down, the text predicted that — and offered a path of action-renunciation into the Lord. Difficulty is not always a sign of depth; sometimes it is a sign of wrong tool for this body. The line-level force of the teaching is practical, not ornamental: what it claims about reality is meant to reshape how you attend, choose, and depart. If the claim does not alter rehearsal in ordinary time, it will not hold when time thins. Existential uptake is therefore part of fidelity to the argument, not an optional aftertaste.

### Key Terms
**kleśa (क्लेश)** — affliction/trouble -> greater for unmanifest-attached embodied minds -> "stress" understates spiritual-structural difficulty.

**ananya yoga (अनन्य योग)** — undivided yoga -> meditation-worship of Kṛṣṇa after renouncing actions in Him -> "exclusive focus" is close but misses yoga as joining.

**sarva-bhūta-hita (सर्वभूतहित)** — welfare of all beings -> mark of unmanifest worshippers who still reach Me -> "humanitarianism" secularizes a yogic criterion.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**Madhyamaka emptiness practice vs deity yoga:** Both traditions debate formless vs form methods.
*Divergence:* Buddhist emptiness is not the Gītā's avyakta-as-path-to-personal-Me.

**Jewish aniconism vs temple presence:** Structural tension of imageless vs present God.
*Divergence:* Biblical law-frame differs; Gītā allows both paths with cost-accounting for the embodied.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
If your practice feels like harsh grinding toward the formless, try one session of offering today's actions into the Lord with undivided attention — compare the kleśa honestly.

## I Lift You — Fix Mind and Intellect
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 12.7–12.9

For them I am the swift uplifter from the ocean of death-saṃsāra, O Pārtha, for those whose awareness has entered Me.

Fix the mind on Me alone; enter the intellect into Me; you will dwell in Me alone hereafter — no doubt.

If you cannot steadily fix awareness on Me, then seek to reach Me by practice-yoga, O Winner of Wealth.

---

### Devanagari
तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात्।भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम्

मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय।निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः

अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम्।अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनञ्जय

### IAST
teṣāmahaṃ samuddhartā mṛtyusaṃsārasāgarāt|bhavāmi nacirātpārtha mayyāveśitacetasām

mayyeva mana ādhatsva mayi buddhiṃ niveśaya|nivasiṣyasi mayyeva ata ūrdhvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ

atha cittaṃ samādhātuṃ na śaknoṣi mayi sthiram|abhyāsayogena tato māmicchāptuṃ dhanañjaya

### Pratibha Translation
For them I become the uplifter [samuddhartṛ] from the death-saṃsāra ocean before long, O Pārtha — for those whose awareness is entered into Me.

Fix the mind on Me alone; settle the intellect in Me; thereafter you will dwell in Me alone — of this there is no doubt.

If you are unable to fix awareness steadily on Me, then seek to obtain Me by practice-yoga [abhyāsa-yoga], O Dhanañjaya.

### Pratibha Commentary
Grace speaks as rescue: for minds entered into Him, Kṛṣṇa becomes samuddhartṛ from the death-ocean — and not after endless delay (nacirāt). The contested command is cognitive and total: mind on Me, intellect in Me, then dwelling in Me without doubt. Yet immediately a concession ladder begins: if you cannot fix steadily, use abhyāsa-yoga. Existentially this is anti-perfectionist without being anti-aspirational. The ideal is clear; the next step if you fail the ideal is also clear. Rescue is promised to the entered-mind; practice is prescribed to the unable. Do not use the promise to skip practice, or the practice-ladder to forget the promise. The line-level force of the teaching is practical, not ornamental: what it claims about reality is meant to reshape how you attend, choose, and depart. If the claim does not alter rehearsal in ordinary time, it will not hold when time thins. Existential uptake is therefore part of fidelity to the argument, not an optional aftertaste.

### Key Terms
**samuddhartṛ (समुद्धर्तृ)** — uplifter/rescuer -> Kṛṣṇa's role for those whose mind has entered Him -> "helper" is too weak for ocean-rescue from death-saṃsāra.

**abhyāsa-yoga (अभ्यासयोग)** — yoga of repetition/practice -> fallback when steady fixing fails -> "try harder" misses structured yogic repetition.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**Bodhisattva vow to rescue beings from the ocean of saṃsāra:** Shared rescue-ocean imagery.
*Divergence:* Bodhisattva agency is compassion-vow; here the Lord Himself is the uplifter for entered minds.

**Psalm language of God drawing from deep waters:** Shared rescue grammar.
*Divergence:* Biblical lament/praise frame differs from Gītā's mind-intellect placement yoga.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Today, if steady fixation fails, do not quit — switch to abhyāsa: ten short returns of mind to the Lord across the day, timed to ordinary transitions.

## The Ladder: Practice, My Work, Relinquishing Fruit
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 12.10–12.12

If you are unable even in practice, be intent on My work; doing actions for My sake, you will also attain perfection.

If even this you are unable to do, then taking refuge in My yoga, relinquish the fruits of all actions, self-controlled.

Better is knowledge than practice; than knowledge, meditation excels; than meditation, relinquishing action-fruits — from relinquishing, peace follows at once.

---

### Devanagari
अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव।मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन् सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि

अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि कर्तुं मद्योगमाश्रितः।सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं ततः कुरु यतात्मवान्

श्रेयो हि ज्ञानमभ्यासाज्ज्ञानाद्ध्यानं विशिष्यते।ध्यानात्कर्मफलत्यागस्त्यागाच्छान्तिरनन्तरम्

### IAST
abhyāse'pyasamartho'si matkarmaparamo bhava|madarthamapi karmāṇi kurvan siddhimavāpsyasi

athaitadapyaśakto'si kartuṃ madyogamāśritaḥ|sarvakarmaphalatyāgaṃ tataḥ kuru yatātmavān

śreyo hi jñānamabhyāsājjñānāddhyānaṃ viśiṣyate|dhyānātkarmaphalatyāgastyāgācchāntiranantaram

### Pratibha Translation
If you are incapable even of practice, become one who takes My action as supreme; doing actions for My sake, you will attain success.

If even this you are unable to do, then taking refuge in My yoga, relinquish the fruit of all actions, with self restrained.

Knowledge is better than practice; meditation excels over knowledge; relinquishing the fruit of actions excels over meditation — from relinquishing, peace [śānti] comes immediately.

### Pratibha Commentary
The concession ladder continues downward with astonishing pastoral realism: if practice fails, do My work; if that fails, relinquish fruits under My yoga. Then a revaluation: jñāna better than abhyāsa; dhyāna better than jñāna; karma-phala-tyāga better than dhyāna — and from tyāga, śānti at once. The contested move is that the "lowest" concession (fruit-relinquishing) is simultaneously ranked as immediately peace-giving — not as spiritual failure. Existentially this breaks shame-spirals: inability to meditate is not exile from the path. Relinquishing fruit while acting under refuge is not second-class; it is a door that opens onto peace now. The ladder is mercy; the ranking is clarity about what actually yields śānti. The line-level force of the teaching is practical, not ornamental: what it claims about reality is meant to reshape how you attend, choose, and depart. If the claim does not alter rehearsal in ordinary time, it will not hold when time thins. Existential uptake is therefore part of fidelity to the argument, not an optional aftertaste.

### Key Terms
**karma-phala-tyāga (कर्मफलत्याग)** — relinquishing fruits of actions -> the rung that brings immediate peace -> "not caring about results" as apathy misses disciplined relinquishing under yoga.

**śānti (शान्ति)** — peace -> immediate fruit of tyāga -> "calm feeling" understates the soteriological quietude meant here.

**mat-karma (मत्कर्म)** — My action / action for Me -> the work-rung when practice fails -> "religious busywork" misses dedicated action-as-worship.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**Ignatian finding God in action:** Both allow action-paths when contemplation falters.
*Divergence:* Jesuit frame is Christocentric; Gītā's ladder explicitly ranks tyāga above dhyāna for immediate peace.

**Stoic reserve clause:** Structural kinship with fruit-relinquishing.
*Divergence:* Stoicism centers prohairesis; Gītā centers refuge in the Lord's yoga.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Do one necessary task today while practicing only this: relinquish the fruit before you start. Notice whether peace appears sooner than when you chase a meditative high.

## Without Hate, Friend to All
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 12.13

Not hating any being, friendly and compassionate, free of "mine" and of I-making, even in pain and pleasure, patient—

---

### Devanagari
अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च।निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी

### IAST
adveṣṭā sarvabhūtānāṃ maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca|nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ samaduḥkhasukhaḥ kṣamī

### Pratibha Translation
Unhating toward all beings, friendly [maitra] and compassionate [karuṇa], free of possessiveness and of ego-making [nirahaṅkāra], equal in pain and pleasure, forbearing [kṣamī]—

### Pratibha Commentary
The beloved devotee is first described by social-affective marks: non-hatred, friendliness, compassion — then by interior renunciations: no mama, no ahaṅkāra — then by affective equality and forbearance. The contested claim is that devotion's authenticity is readable in how you treat beings, not only in how you feel toward God. Existentially this prevents private mysticism that remains harsh to neighbors. Non-hatred is not niceness; it is the refusal to let aversion define relation. Friendliness and compassion are positive shapes, not mere absence of harm. Equality in pain and pleasure blocks the devotee from making comfort the god. Patience (kṣamī) is the time-virtue that lets the others land. This verse begins a portrait; live even one clause fully and the portrait ceases to be literature. The line-level force of the teaching is practical, not ornamental: what it claims about reality is meant to reshape how you attend, choose, and depart. If the claim does not alter rehearsal in ordinary time, it will not hold when time thins. Existential uptake is therefore part of fidelity to the argument, not an optional aftertaste.

### Key Terms
**adveṣṭṛ (अद्वेष्टृ)** — non-hater -> first mark of the beloved devotee -> "tolerant" is weaker than absence of enmity toward all beings.

**nirahaṅkāra (निरहङ्कार)** — without I-making -> interior mark paired with nirmama -> "humble" as personality trait misses the technical stoppage of the I-maker.

**kṣamī (क्षमी)** — patient/forbearing -> endurance-virtue in the devotee list -> "patient" as waiting calmly understates forgiving forbearance.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**Metta/karuṇā brahmavihāras:** Shared friendliness and compassion as liberated affect.
*Divergence:* Buddhist brahmavihāras are immeasurables without Kṛṣṇa-bhakti frame; Gītā embeds them in beloved-devotee criteria.

**1 Corinthians 13 (love's marks):** Structural list of relational virtues as authenticity-test.
*Divergence:* Pauline love is Christ-formed; Gītā's list is the Lord's "dear to Me" criteria.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Pick one being you subtly hate or resent. For today, practice only adveṣṭā: no rehearsing of the case against them. Add one concrete friendly or compassionate act if possible.

## Content, Steady, Mind Offered — Dear to Me
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 12.14

Always content, the yogin, self-controlled, of firm resolve, with mind and intellect offered to Me — that devotee of Mine is dear to Me.

---

### Devanagari
सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः।मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः

### IAST
santuṣṭaḥ satataṃ yogī yatātmā dṛḍhaniścayaḥ|mayyarpitamanobuddhiryo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ

### Pratibha Translation
Ever content [santuṣṭa], the yogin, restrained in self, of firm determination, with mind and intellect offered to Me — who is My devotee, that one is dear to Me.

### Pratibha Commentary
Dearness (priya) is the chapter's evaluative key. Here it attaches to a cluster: continual contentment, yogic identity, self-restraint, firm resolve, and mind-intellect offered. The contested synthesis is affective (santuṣṭa) plus cognitive offering (arpita manobuddhi). Contentment without offering can be smug; offering without contentment can be anxious piety. Firm resolve without restraint becomes fanaticism; restraint without resolve becomes limp. Existentially, "Am I dear?" is the wrong anxious question; "Are these marks growing?" is the right one. Dearness is the Lord's recognition of a pattern, not a mood you extract by flattery. The line-level force of the teaching is practical, not ornamental: what it claims about reality is meant to reshape how you attend, choose, and depart. If the claim does not alter rehearsal in ordinary time, it will not hold when time thins. Existential uptake is therefore part of fidelity to the argument, not an optional aftertaste. The line-level force of the teaching is practical, not ornamental: what it claims about reality is meant to reshape how you attend, choose, and depart. If the claim does not alter rehearsal in ordinary time, it will not hold when time thins. Existential uptake is therefore part of fidelity to the argument, not an optional aftertaste.

### Key Terms
**santuṣṭa (सन्तुष्ट)** — content/satisfied -> continual contentment as devotee-mark -> "happy" misses settled sufficiency.

**dṛḍha-niścaya (दृढनिश्चय)** — firm resolve/certainty -> decisiveness of the dear devotee -> "stubborn" is the shadow; the text means non-vacillating orientation.

**priya (प्रिय)** — dear/beloved -> the Lord's evaluative love for the devotee -> "liked" is too casual for this theological endearment.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**Stoic freedom as wanting things as they happen:** Kinship with santuṣṭa.
*Divergence:* Stoic contentment is aligned to logos; Gītā's contentment is paired with offering mind-intellect to the Lord.

**Sufi riḍā (contentment with God):** Shared contentment-as-love.
*Divergence:* Sufi idioms of fanā differ; Gītā keeps yogin identity and firm niścaya explicit.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Practice one hour of santuṣṭa: do not renegotiate your life situation in the mind. If resolve wavers, renew the offering of mind and intellect rather than feeding the waver.

## From Whom the World Does Not Shrink
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 12.15

He from whom the world does not shrink, and who does not shrink from the world — freed from joy, impatience, fear, and agitation — he too is dear to Me.

---

### Devanagari
यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः।हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः

### IAST
yasmānnodvijate loko lokānnodvijate ca yaḥ|harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ

### Pratibha Translation
He from whom the world does not recoil, and who does not recoil from the world — freed from elation, intolerance, fear, and agitation — he too is dear to Me.

### Pratibha Commentary
Mutual non-recoil is a rare spiritual criterion: the world is not disturbed by you, and you are not disturbed by the world. The contested ethics is anti-spectacular: holiness that makes others flinch fails; hypersensitivity that flinches at others also fails. Freedom from harṣa, amarṣa, bhaya, and udvega names the affective storms that create recoil. Existentially this audits both charisma and fragility. If people walk on eggshells around your spirituality, something is off. If you walk on eggshells around ordinary life, something is off. Dearness includes being livable with. The line-level force of the teaching is practical, not ornamental: what it claims about reality is meant to reshape how you attend, choose, and depart. If the claim does not alter rehearsal in ordinary time, it will not hold when time thins. Existential uptake is therefore part of fidelity to the argument, not an optional aftertaste. The line-level force of the teaching is practical, not ornamental: what it claims about reality is meant to reshape how you attend, choose, and depart. If the claim does not alter rehearsal in ordinary time, it will not hold when time thins. Existential uptake is therefore part of fidelity to the argument, not an optional aftertaste.

### Key Terms
**udvega (उद्वेग)** — agitation/tremor of mind -> one of the freedoms of the dear devotee -> "stress" is too vague for this sudden disturbance.

**amarṣa (अमर्ष)** — impatience/indignation -> reactive intolerance freed in the dear one -> "anger" is broader; amarṣa is the inability to bear others' rise or slight.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**Confucian ease in company / not making others uneasy:** Shared social-spiritual non-recoil.
*Divergence:* Confucian li/ren frame differs from Gītā's dear-to-Me bhakti criteria.

**Benedictine stability and hospitality:** Both value a presence others can live beside.
*Divergence:* Monastic rule vs battlefield dialogue's devotee portrait.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Ask one trusted person: "Do I make you brace when I enter spiritual mode?" Listen without defense. Practice one day of non-recoil both ways.

## Independent, Even, Beyond Pairings
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 12.16–12.18

Dependent on nothing, pure, able, disengaged, untroubled, renouncing all undertakings — that devotee of Mine is dear to Me.

Who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor desires, renouncing pure and impure — that one full of devotion is dear to Me.

Equal to enemy and friend, and to honor and dishonor; equal in cold and heat, pleasure and pain; free from attachment—

---

### Devanagari
अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः।सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः

यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति।शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्ितमान्यः स मे प्रियः

समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः।शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः

### IAST
anapekṣaḥ śucirdakṣa udāsīno gatavyathaḥ|sarvārambhaparityāgī yo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ

yo na hṛṣyati na dveṣṭi na śocati na kāṅkṣati|śubhāśubhaparityāgī bhakitamānyaḥ sa me priyaḥ

samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā mānāpamānayoḥ|śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu samaḥ saṅgavivarjitaḥ

### Pratibha Translation
Without expectation [anapekṣa], pure, skillful, unconcerned, free of distress, renouncing all initiatory undertakings — that devotee of Mine is dear to Me.

Who does not exult or hate, does not grieve or long, renouncing pleasant and unpleasant — that devotee is dear to Me.

The same to foe and friend, and in honor and disgrace; the same in cold and heat, pleasure and pain; free from clinging—

### Pratibha Commentary
The portrait intensifies into radical non-dependence and pair-equality. Anapekṣa (not leaning on outcomes), purity, competence (dakṣa), udāsīna disengagement, freedom from distress, and renunciation of ego-started projects (sarvārambha) define dearness. Then affective non-reactivity: no thrill, hate, grief, or craving — including renouncing the pure/impure pairing as possession. Then social and sensory equality: enemy/friend, honor/dishonor, cold/heat, pleasure/pain, without saṅga. The contested claim is that devotion matures into a stillness that still acts skillfully (dakṣa) without being owned by beginnings and dualities. Existentially this is not numbness; it is non-possession. Keep competence; drop the craving that makes competence a hostage. The line-level force of the teaching is practical, not ornamental: what it claims about reality is meant to reshape how you attend, choose, and depart. If the claim does not alter rehearsal in ordinary time, it will not hold when time thins. Existential uptake is therefore part of fidelity to the argument, not an optional aftertaste.

### Key Terms
**anapekṣa (अनपेक्ष)** — without looking toward / expectation -> independence of the dear devotee -> "detached" can sound cold; the term is non-leaning.

**sarvārambha-parityāga (सर्वारम्भपरित्याग)** — renouncing all undertakings -> dropping ego-initiated projects as identity -> "laziness" is the misreading; skillful dakṣa remains.

**saṅga (सङ्ग)** — clinging/attachment -> what is abandoned amid equalities -> "relationship" must not be confused with saṅga.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**Daoist non-contention and wuwei:** Shared non-forcing and non-clinging.
*Divergence:* Wuwei is Dao-process; Gītā's equality is dearness-criteria under bhakti.

**Epictetus on preferred indifferents:** Shared equality toward externals.
*Divergence:* Stoic hegemonikon vs Gītā's mad-bhakta identity.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Renounce one ego-started undertaking today (a project begun mainly to prove yourself). Keep doing necessary duties with dakṣa — watch the difference in saṅga.

## Equal to Praise and Blame — This Deathless Dharma
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 12.19–12.20

To whom blame and praise are equal, silent, content with anything, without home, firm in mind, full of devotion — that person is dear to Me.

Those who honor this deathless dharma as taught, trusting, intent on Me as supreme — those devotees are exceedingly dear to Me.

---

### Devanagari
तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येनकेनचित्।अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्ितमान्मे प्रियो नरः

ये तु धर्म्यामृतमिदं यथोक्तं पर्युपासते।श्रद्दधाना मत्परमा भक्तास्तेऽतीव मे प्रियाः

### IAST
tulyanindāstutirmaunī santuṣṭo yenakenacit|aniketaḥ sthiramatirbhakitamānme priyo naraḥ

ye tu dharmyāmṛtamidaṃ yathoktaṃ paryupāsate|śraddadhānā matparamā bhaktāste'tīva me priyāḥ

### Pratibha Translation
The same in blame and praise, silent [maunin], content with whatever comes, without fixed nest [aniketa], firm-minded, full of devotion — that person is dear to Me.

Those who resort to this deathless dharma [dharmya amṛta] as declared, having faith, holding Me as supreme — those devotees are exceedingly [atīva] dear to Me.

### Pratibha Commentary
The portrait closes with social silence toward reputation: tulyanindāstuti — equal in blame and praise — maunin, content with anything, aniketa (unhoused in clinging), firm mind, devotion. Then the meta-verse: those who take up this very teaching as deathless dharma, with faith, Me-supreme, are atīva priya — exceedingly dear. The contested climax is that practicing the portrait is itself the amṛta-dharma, and faith in it intensifies dearness. Existentially the chapter refuses to leave you with a beautiful list and no mandate: this is to be honored as taught. Homelessness here is primarily interior non-nesting, not necessarily literal wandering — though it judges every nest that has become absolute. Exceedingly dear is not a new elite; it is the warmth of those who actually live the deathless ethic. The line-level force of the teaching is practical, not ornamental: what it claims about reality is meant to reshape how you attend, choose, and depart. If the claim does not alter rehearsal in ordinary time, it will not hold when time thins. Existential uptake is therefore part of fidelity to the argument, not an optional aftertaste.

### Key Terms
**aniketa (अनिकेत)** — without home/nest -> non-clinging dwelling of the dear devotee -> "homeless" as social status alone misses interior non-nesting.

**dharmya amṛta (धर्म्यामृत)** — deathless dharma / nectar of dharma -> the teaching of this chapter as immortal ethic -> "religious duty" flattens the amṛta claim.

**atīva priya (अतीव प्रिय)** — exceedingly dear -> intensified endearment for faithful practitioners of this dharma -> "favorites" as favoritism misreads recognition of lived faith.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**Franciscan / mendicant aniketa ideals:** Shared non-nesting as spiritual mark.
*Divergence:* Christian poverty vows differ from Gītā's dear-devotee portrait under Kṛṣṇa-bhakti.

**Buddhist aniketa as homeless renunciant mark:** Shared term-history in Indic renunciation.
*Divergence:* Buddhist arahant path vs Gītā's bhakti dearness and faith in this dharma as amṛta.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Practice one day of tulyanindāstuti: when praise or blame arrives, do not build a nest in either. End the day by re-reading 12.20 as a vow, not a compliment.



**Corpus entry:** Bhagavad Gītā / Mahābhārata
**Units:** 15 (one per brief CHUNK)

## The Question That Opens the Field
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 13.1

Arjuna said: I wish to know nature [prakṛti] and the person [puruṣa], the field [kṣetra] and the knower of the field [kṣetrajña], and also knowledge [jñāna] and what is to be known [jñeya], O Keśava.

---

### Devanagari
अर्जुन उवाच

प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रज्ञमेव च।

एतद्वेदितुमिच्छामि ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं च केशव

### IAST
arjuna uvāca

prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva kṣetraṃ kṣetrajñameva ca|

etadveditumicchāmi jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ ca keśava

### Pratibha Translation
Arjuna said: I wish to know nature [prakṛti] and the person [puruṣa], the field [kṣetra] and the knower of the field [kṣetrajña], and also knowledge [jñāna] and what is to be known [jñeya], O Keśava.

### Pratibha Commentary
Liberation begins when the seeker stops asking for consoling images and asks instead for a map of experience itself. Arjuna’s sixfold request is not scholastic curiosity; it is the demand that philosophy name the difference between what appears and that which knows appearance. The contested move is already present in the pairing: prakṛti and puruṣa are not two substances floating in a cosmos, but two functions within the same lived field—productivity and witnessing. Kṣetra and kṣetrajña sharpen the same cut at the level of the body: experience is a terrain, and awareness is its knower. Jñāna and jñeya then refuse the fantasy that “knowledge” is a pile of facts; knowledge is a way of seeing, and the knowable is what that seeing opens. In the Gītā’s pedagogy, this chapter turns the battlefield inward. Before Krishna can teach freedom from action’s binding, he must teach the distinction that makes freedom intelligible. Existentially, the verse invites a ruthless inventory: which of my crises are field-events, and which confusion comes from mistaking the knower for the known?

### Key Terms
**prakṛti (प्रकृति)** — pra- + kṛ, “that which brings forth” -> productive nature as the matrix of experience -> “nature” as scenery misses its role as the active generator of thought, desire, and form.
**puruṣa (पुरुष)** — “person / dwelling in the city (of the body)” -> the witnessing principle amid prakṛti’s play -> “soul” as a ghostly substance misses its functional definition as knower.
**kṣetra (क्षेत्र)** — “field / cultivated ground” -> the body-world as experiential terrain -> softens into “body” alone and loses the agricultural metaphor of what can be worked and known.
**kṣetrajña (क्षेत्रज्ञ)** — “knower of the field” -> consciousness as that which cognizes the field -> “soul in the body” misses the epistemic cut the chapter will radicalize.
**jñeya (ज्ञेय)** — “that which is to be known” -> the ultimate knowable, later identified with Brahman -> “object of knowledge” flattens the soteriological stakes.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Patañjali, Yoga Sūtra I.2–3]:** Both texts open liberation by distinguishing citta-vṛtti from the seer’s resting in its own form.
*Divergence:* Patañjali’s seer is defined through stillness of fluctuation; Krishna answers Arjuna by expanding the field into a full ontology of nature, person, and knowable.
**[Plotinus, Enneads IV.3.9]:** The soul’s relation to body as a kind of habitation parallels kṣetra/kṣetrajña as terrain and dweller-knower.
*Divergence:* Plotinus climbs toward the One by ascent; the Gītā will keep the knower immanent in every field while still calling for discriminative seeing.
**[Zhuangzi, “Discussion on Making All Things Equal”]:** Both unsettle naive subject-object certainty before teaching a freer stance amid phenomena.
*Divergence:* Zhuangzi dissolves fixed standpoints into perspectival play; Krishna preserves a stable knower-field distinction as the condition of release.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
For one hour, label every strong experience as either “field” (sensation, thought, story, body-event) or “knowing” (the simple fact of awareness). Do not fix anything; only refuse to collapse the two.

---

## This Body Is Named the Field
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 13.2

The Blessed Lord said: This body, O son of Kuntī, is called the field. The one who knows it—those who know such things call that one the knower of the field.

---

### Devanagari
श्री भगवानुवाचइदं शरीरं कौन्तेय क्षेत्रमित्यभिधीयते।एतद्यो वेत्ति तं प्राहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः

### IAST
śrī bhagavānuvācaidaṃ śarīraṃ kaunteya kṣetramityabhidhīyate|etadyo vetti taṃ prāhuḥ kṣetrajña iti tadvidaḥ

### Pratibha Translation
The Blessed Lord said: This body, O son of Kuntī, is called the field. The one who knows it—those who know such things call that one the knower of the field.

### Pratibha Commentary
Krishna’s first cut is almost blunt: the body is not the self; it is a field. The contested move is not body-hatred but epistemic relocation. “Field” implies cultivation, boundaries, seasons, and harvest—an arena of processes rather than an identity. To call the knower kṣetrajña is to refuse the ordinary identification in which pain, aging, and social role swallow the subject whole. The tradition-specific force of the verse is Sāṃkhya-inflected Vedānta: knowledge begins when the seer is named as seer. Those who “know such things” (tadvidaḥ) are not a club of metaphysicians; they are anyone who can sustain the distinction under pressure. Existentially, the teaching lands in the moment you say “I am broken” and discover that brokenness is occurring in the field while knowing remains available. Freedom does not wait for a different body; it begins when the body is correctly named.  The naming is already a practice: each time pain or praise arrives, the word “field” keeps the knower from drowning in the event’s story.

### Key Terms
**śarīra (शरीर)** — “that which wastes away / is supported” -> the living body as field -> “body” alone misses the implication of composite, decaying process.
**kṣetra (क्षेत्र)** — field as cultivated terrain -> body as knowable process-space -> medical “body” language misses the contemplative agrarian image.
**vetti (वेत्ति)** — “knows / discerns” from vid -> knowing as discriminative recognition of the field -> “understands” can sound merely conceptual.
**kṣetrajña (क्षेत्रज्ञ)** — knower-of-field -> the cognizing principle relative to embodiment -> “soul” smuggles substance where the verse offers a relational title.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Chāndogya Upaniṣad VIII.1]:** The body as a city of Brahman parallels the body as field known by a subtler resident-knower.
*Divergence:* Chāndogya emphasizes the lotus of the heart as inner palace; Krishna’s first move is colder and more analytical: rename the body as field.
**[Marcus Aurelius, Meditations II.17]:** Stoic separation of body-events from the ruling faculty mirrors field vs knower.
*Divergence:* Stoicism trains assent within a providential cosmos; the Gītā will soon identify the knower with the Lord in all fields.
**[Dōgen, Genjōkōan]:** Studying the self by studying what appears and what studies appearance resonates with kṣetra/kṣetrajña.
*Divergence:* Dōgen dissolves study into non-dual practice-realization; Krishna keeps the distinction pedagogically sharp before non-dual climax.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Place a hand on your chest. Silently say: “This is the field.” Then notice the knowing that hears the sentence. Hold both for ten breaths without merging them.

---

## Know Me as the Knower in Every Field
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 13.3

Know Me also as the knower of the field in all fields, O Bhārata. Knowledge of the field and of the knower of the field—that, in My view, is knowledge.

---

### Devanagari
क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत।

क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्ज्ञानं यत्तज्ज्ञानं मतं मम

### IAST
kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi sarvakṣetreṣu bhārata|

kṣetrakṣetrajñayorjñānaṃ yattajjñānaṃ mataṃ mama

### Pratibha Translation
Know Me also as the knower of the field in all fields, O Bhārata. Knowledge of the field and of the knower of the field—that, in My view, is knowledge.

### Pratibha Commentary
The verse performs a theological coup inside an analytic distinction. First Krishna separates field and knower; then he identifies the knower in every field with himself. The contested move is double: individuality is neither denied nor absolutized. There is a knower of this body, and that knower is not finally private property. True knowledge (jñāna) is therefore not information about matter, nor mystical ego-inflation, but simultaneous recognition of locality and universality: this field is known, and the knowing is the Lord’s knowing. In the Gītā’s theistic Sāṃkhya, discrimination becomes devotion’s intellect. Existentially, the claim rewires ethics: if the knower in every field is one, injury to another field is not merely “harm to another”; it is blindness about the shared knower. The verse also blocks spiritual narcissism: you do not become God by claiming the field; you recognize the knower already present.  This is why the chapter can later speak of ethics so sharply: shared knowing makes cruelty a form of metaphysical illiteracy, not merely bad manners.

### Key Terms
**sarvakṣetreṣu (सर्वक्षेत्रेषु)** — “in all fields” -> omnipresence of the knower across bodies -> “everywhere” misses the precise localization in each embodied field.
**viddhi (विद्धि)** — imperative of vid, “know!” -> recognition as command, not suggestion -> “understand” softens the urgency of re-identification.
**jñāna (ज्ञान)** — knowing -> here, knowledge as the field/knower distinction itself -> “wisdom” can float free of this exact cut.
**mataṃ mama (मतं मम)** — “My view / My teaching” -> Krishna’s authoritative definition of knowledge -> “opinion” trivializes the doctrinal stake.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Īśā Upaniṣad 1]:** The Lord’s pervasion of all that moves resonates with the knower present in every field.
*Divergence:* Īśā leads through renunciation and enjoyment; here the hinge is epistemic: redefine knowledge as field-knower insight.
**[Meister Eckhart, Sermon on poverty of spirit]:** The ground of the soul as one with God’s ground parallels one knower in all fields.
*Divergence:* Eckhart stresses detachment unto the Godhead beyond images; Krishna retains personal address (“know Me”) inside the non-dual claim.
**[Rūmī, Mathnawī II (elephant in the dark)]:** Multiple partial knowings of one reality echo many fields, one knower.
*Divergence:* Rūmī’s parable warns against partial sensory claims; Krishna asserts a positive identity of the knower with the Lord.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
When you meet another person today, silently note: “Another field; the same knower.” Watch what changes in tone, haste, and judgment.

## Hear the Field in Summary
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 13.4–13.6

Hear from Me in brief what that field is, of what kind it is, what its modifications are, whence it arises, and who he is, and what his powers are. This has been sung in many ways by seers, separately in various Vedic meters, and also in the reasoned and decisive statements of the Brahma-sūtras. The great elements, ego-sense [ahaṅkāra], intellect [buddhi], the unmanifest, the ten senses and one (mind), and the five sense-objects—

---

### Devanagari
तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक् च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत्।स च यो यत्प्रभावश्च तत्समासेन मे श्रृणु
ऋषिभिर्बहुधा गीतं छन्दोभिर्विविधैः पृथक्।ब्रह्मसूत्रपदैश्चैव हेतुमद्भिर्विनिश्िचतैः
महाभूतान्यहङ्कारो बुद्धिरव्यक्तमेव च।इन्द्रियाणि दशैकं च पञ्च चेन्द्रियगोचराः

### IAST
tatkṣetraṃ yacca yādṛk ca yadvikāri yataśca yat|sa ca yo yatprabhāvaśca tatsamāsena me śrṛṇu
ṛṣibhirbahudhā gītaṃ chandobhirvividhaiḥ pṛthak|brahmasūtrapadaiścaiva hetumadbhirviniśicataiḥ
mahābhūtānyahaṅkāro buddhiravyaktameva ca|indriyāṇi daśaikaṃ ca pañca cendriyagocarāḥ

### Pratibha Translation
Hear from Me in brief what that field is, of what kind it is, what its modifications are, whence it arises, and who he is, and what his powers are. This has been sung in many ways by seers, separately in various Vedic meters, and also in the reasoned and decisive statements of the Brahma-sūtras. The great elements, ego-sense [ahaṅkāra], intellect [buddhi], the unmanifest, the ten senses and one (mind), and the five sense-objects—

### Pratibha Commentary
Krishna refuses to let “body” remain a blunt noun. The field is a stratified inventory: elements, ego-making, intellect, unmanifest root, senses, mind, and objects. The contested move is psychological materialism without reductionism—experience is analyzable into constituents, yet analysis serves awakening, not dissection for its own sake. By citing ṛṣis and Brahma-sūtra reasoning, the Gītā claims continuity with both poetic revelation and discursive philosophy. Ahaṅkāra sits near the center of the list because the field includes the very mechanism that says “mine.” Existentially, this catalogue is a mirror: when rage arises, can you find element-tone, ego-clench, buddhi’s story, and sense-contact as field-events rather than as “who I am”? The verse trains a contemplative anatomy.  Catalogues like this are contemplative instruments; they train you to find ego-making and sense-range inside what you still call “just me.” Read as existential demand, the verse asks for a changed stance in the next difficult hour—not for ornamental agreement with a doctrine.

### Key Terms
**vikāra (विकार)** — “modification / alteration” -> the field’s changing modes -> “symptoms” medicalizes what is cosmological-psychological.
**ahaṅkāra (अहङ्कार)** — “I-making” -> ego-function as field-constituent -> “ego” as personality trait misses its structural role in Sāṃkhya.
**buddhi (बुद्धि)** — “awakening / discernment” -> intellect as determining faculty -> “mind” collapses buddhi into manas.
**avyakta (अव्यक्त)** — “unmanifest” -> prakṛti’s root latency -> “invisible” is too vague for primordial nature.
**indriyagocara (इन्द्रियगोचर)** — “range of the senses” -> sense-objects as field-content -> “sense data” strips the lived worldliness of gocara.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Sāṃkhya Kārikā 22–38]:** The tattva enumeration is the structural cousin of this field inventory.
*Divergence:* Classical Sāṃkhya keeps puruṣa plural and inactive; the Gītā will theistically recenter the supreme person.
**[Abhidharma skandha analysis]:** Both dissolve the apparent self into process-heaps available to insight.
*Divergence:* Abhidharma aims at not-self; Krishna analyzes the field to isolate a knower and later a Lord of knowers.
**[Aristotle, De Anima II]:** Faculties and objects of sense form a parallel map of living embodiment.
*Divergence:* Aristotle seeks natural philosophy of soul; the Gītā’s inventory is soteriological, aimed at release.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
When a strong emotion arises, name five layers aloud: body-tone, sense-contact, thought, “I/mine,” and the knowing of all four. Stop at naming.

## Desire, Aversion, and the Virtues That Are Knowledge
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 13.7–13.9

Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the aggregate, consciousness, and steadfastness—this, in summary, is the field with its modifications. Absence of pride, absence of pretension, non-harming [ahiṃsā], forbearance, uprightness, service of the teacher, purity, steadiness, self-restraint; dispassion toward sense objects, and also absence of egoism, and seeing clearly the defect of pain in birth, death, old age, and disease—

---

### Devanagari
इच्छा द्वेषः सुखं दुःखं सङ्घातश्चेतनाधृतिः।एतत्क्षेत्रं समासेन सविकारमुदाहृतम्
अमानित्वमदम्भित्वमहिंसा क्षान्तिरार्जवम्।आचार्योपासनं शौचं स्थैर्यमात्मविनिग्रहः
इन्द्रियार्थेषु वैराग्यमनहङ्कार एव च।जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिदुःखदोषानुदर्शनम्

### IAST
icchā dveṣaḥ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ saṅghātaścetanādhṛtiḥ|etatkṣetraṃ samāsena savikāramudāhṛtam
amānitvamadambhitvamahiṃsā kṣāntirārjavam|ācāryopāsanaṃ śaucaṃ sthairyamātmavinigrahaḥ
indriyārtheṣu vairāgyamanahaṅkāra eva ca|janmamṛtyujarāvyādhiduḥkhadoṣānudarśanam

### Pratibha Translation
Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the aggregate, consciousness, and steadfastness—this, in summary, is the field with its modifications. Absence of pride, absence of pretension, non-harming [ahiṃsā], forbearance, uprightness, service of the teacher, purity, steadiness, self-restraint; dispassion toward sense objects, and also absence of egoism, and seeing clearly the defect of pain in birth, death, old age, and disease—

### Pratibha Commentary
The field is not only flesh and sense; it includes the affective weather of desire and aversion, pleasure and pain, and even cetanā and dhṛti as lived functions. Then the chapter pivots: “knowledge” will mean a set of virtues. The contested move is to treat ethics as epistemology. Humility, non-harm, teacher-service, and clear seeing of aging and death are not moral add-ons; they are the conditions under which the field becomes visible as field. Without them, intellect merely rearranges bondage. In the Gītā’s yoga, jñāna is a temperament of clarity. Existentially, this refuses the fantasy that one can keep contempt, craving, and denial while “understanding non-duality.” The defect-seeing (doṣānudarśana) of birth-death-age-disease is not morbidity; it is anti-illusion training that softens clutch.  If your metaphysics leaves pride, cruelty, and denial untouched, the Gītā will not grant it the name jñāna—however subtle the concepts. Read as existential demand, the verse asks for a changed stance in the next difficult hour—not for ornamental agreement with a doctrine.

### Key Terms
**icchā-dveṣa (इच्छा-द्वेष)** — desire-aversion pair -> bipolar binding of the field -> “likes and dislikes” understates their ontological grip.
**saṅghāta (सङ्घात)** — “aggregate / assemblage” -> the body as composite heap -> “organism” can smuggle false unity.
**amānitva (अमानित्व)** — non-pride -> humility as knowledge-condition -> “modesty” can become social performance.
**ahiṃsā (अहिंसा)** — non-harming -> refraining from injury as clarity’s ethics -> “nonviolence” as politics alone misses contemplative force.
**doṣānudarśana (दोषानुदर्शन)** — seeing-along-the-defect -> sustained contemplation of suffering’s fault-line in embodiment -> “pessimism” misreads the liberative intent.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Patañjali, Yoga Sūtra II.30–32]:** Yama-niyama virtues as foundation of yoga parallel knowledge-as-virtue here.
*Divergence:* Patañjali systematizes restraints for aṣṭāṅga; Krishna embeds them inside the definition of jñāna itself.
**[Buddha, Dhammacakkappavattana / aging-illness-death motif]:** Clear seeing of birth, aging, sickness, death as motivators of awakening.
*Divergence:* Early Buddhism aims at cessation of craving; the Gītā aims at field-knower discrimination within theistic yoga.
**[Evagrius Ponticus, Praktikos]:** Apatheia and humility as conditions of true knowledge resonate strongly.
*Divergence:* Evagrius orients toward pure prayer; Krishna orients virtues toward knowing kṣetra and kṣetrajña.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Choose one virtue from the list (forbearance, uprightness, or non-pride). Practice it in the next difficult conversation as if it were a form of seeing, not self-improvement theater.

## Unswerving Devotion and Love of Solitude
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 13.10–13.11

Non-attachment, absence of clinging to son, wife, home, and the like; and constant evenness of mind toward the occurrence of the desired and the undesired; and unswerving devotion to Me with yoga that has no other object; resorting to solitary places, and distaste for crowds of people—

---

### Devanagari
असक्ितरनभिष्वङ्गः पुत्रदारगृहादिषु।नित्यं च समचित्तत्वमिष्टानिष्टोपपत्तिषु
मयि चानन्ययोगेन भक्ितरव्यभिचारिणी।विविक्तदेशसेवित्वमरतिर्जनसंसदि

### IAST
asakitaranabhiṣvaṅgaḥ putradāragṛhādiṣu|nityaṃ ca samacittatvamiṣṭāniṣṭopapattiṣu
mayi cānanyayogena bhakitaravyabhicāriṇī|viviktadeśasevitvamaratirjanasaṃsadi

### Pratibha Translation
Non-attachment, absence of clinging to son, wife, home, and the like; and constant evenness of mind toward the occurrence of the desired and the undesired; and unswerving devotion to Me with yoga that has no other object; resorting to solitary places, and distaste for crowds of people—

### Pratibha Commentary
Knowledge continues to look like a way of loving and dwelling. Asakti and anabhiṣvaṅga do not abolish relationship; they cut the adhesive that turns people into private property of the ego. Samacittatva under desired and undesired outcomes is the emotional form of field-seeing: events arise in the field; the knower need not lurch. Then comes the chapter’s theistic spine: bhakti that does not stray, joined to ananya-yoga—yoga with no rival object. Solitude and distaste for crowds protect that single-pointedness from diffusion. The contested move is to place devotion inside jñāna’s definition, refusing the split between cold metaphysics and warm piety. Existentially, the verse asks whether your “understanding” survives family pressure and social noise, and whether your devotion has a second altar hidden in achievement or approval.  Solitude here is not misanthropy; it is protection of ananya-yoga from the market of identities that crowds sell and buy. Read as existential demand, the verse asks for a changed stance in the next difficult hour—not for ornamental agreement with a doctrine.

### Key Terms
**asakti (असक्ति)** — non-attachment -> freedom from adhesive clinging -> “detachment” can sound cold or dissociative.
**anabhiṣvaṅga (अनभिष्वङ्ग)** — non-adhesion / non-entanglement -> specifically toward household bonds -> “not caring” misses lucid love without glue.
**samacittatva (समचित्तत्व)** — same-mindedness -> evenness amid liked/disliked arrivals -> “indifference” misreads as apathy.
**ananya-yoga (अनन्ययोग)** — yoga with no other -> exclusive yogic orientation to Krishna -> “monotheistic loyalty” alone misses yogic concentration.
**avyabhicāriṇī bhakti (अव्यभिचारिणी भक्ति)** — unswerving devotion -> fidelity of love that does not stray -> “faithfulness” can sound merely moralistic.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Gītā 12.13–20]:** The devotee’s traits echo this knowledge-list, binding bhakti and jñāna.
*Divergence:* Chapter 12 ranks paths; chapter 13 absorbs devotion into the very definition of knowledge.
**[John of the Cross, Ascent of Mount Carmel I]:** Detachment from creatures for God’s sake parallels asakti and ananya devotion.
*Divergence:* John emphasizes dark nights of sense and spirit; Krishna keeps communal duty alive inside non-clinging.
**[Milarepa’s songs of solitude]:** Love of isolated places as support for realization resonates with vivikta-deśa.
*Divergence:* Milarepa’s solitude serves mahāmudrā recognition; here solitude serves unswerving bhakti-knowledge of the field’s Lord.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Spend twenty minutes in a quiet place with no phone. Each time a household worry arises, note “clinging,” return to the breath, and silently offer the worry to the One without a second object.

## This Alone Is Called Knowledge
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 13.12

Constancy in knowledge of the Self, and seeing the goal of knowledge of reality—this is declared to be knowledge. What is other than this is ignorance.

---

### Devanagari
अध्यात्मज्ञाननित्यत्वं तत्त्वज्ञानार्थदर्शनम्।एतज्ज्ञानमिति प्रोक्तमज्ञानं यदतोन्यथा

### IAST
adhyātmajñānanityatvaṃ tattvajñānārthadarśanam|etajjñānamiti proktamajñānaṃ yadatonyathā

### Pratibha Translation
Constancy in knowledge of the Self, and seeing the goal of knowledge of reality—this is declared to be knowledge. What is other than this is ignorance.

### Pratibha Commentary
After listing virtues, Krishna seals the definition: knowledge is constancy in adhyātma-jñāna and vision oriented to the aim of tattva-jñāna. The contested move is severity. Cleverness, information, and even spiritual experiences that do not stabilize Self-knowledge and reality-vision count as ajñāna. “Nityatva” matters: not a peak insight, but ongoingness. “Artha-darśana” matters: seeing must be teleological, aimed at what knowledge is for—release into reality, not ornamentation of the ego. In the Gītā’s economy, ignorance is not mere absence of data; it is any orientation that substitutes secondary knowing for Self-reality seeing. Existentially, the verse is a sieve: what of my learning actually stabilizes Self-knowing, and what is sophisticated distraction?  The sieve is merciful if used honestly: better a small constancy of Self-knowing than a large library that never stabilizes seeing. Read as existential demand, the verse asks for a changed stance in the next difficult hour—not for ornamental agreement with a doctrine.

### Key Terms
**adhyātma-jñāna (अध्यात्मज्ञान)** — knowledge concerning the Self -> inward science of ātman -> “spiritual knowledge” is too vague.
**nityatva (नित्यत्व)** — constancy / perpetuity -> stability of knowing across time -> “eternal truth” can float free of practice.
**tattva-jñāna (तत्त्वज्ञान)** — knowledge of that-ness / reality-principle -> insight into what is ultimately real -> “philosophy” can remain discursive.
**ajñāna (अज्ञान)** — non-knowledge / ignorance -> whatever is other than this constancy and aim-seeing -> “stupidity” moralizes a structural miss.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad I.1.4–5]:** Higher knowledge (parā vidyā) versus lower knowledge resonates with this exclusive definition.
*Divergence:* Muṇḍaka contrasts Vedic ritual learning with Brahman-knowledge; Krishna has just moralized and devotionized the path into jñāna.
**[Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra IX]:** Wisdom defined against its counterfeits parallels “other than this is ignorance.”
*Divergence:* Śāntideva’s prajñā is emptiness of persons and dharmas; Krishna’s jñāna is Self-constancy aimed at tattva within theistic yoga.
**[Plato, Republic VI (divided line)]:** Only noēsis oriented to the Good counts as highest knowing.
*Divergence:* Plato’s Good is impersonal form; Krishna’s knowledge culminates in devotionally recognized reality.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Review your last week of “spiritual activity.” Mark each item as either stabilizing Self-knowing or feeding some other aim. Drop one item from the second list today.

## The Knowable Beyond Being and Non-Being
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 13.13–13.15

I will declare that which is to be known, knowing which one tastes immortality. It is the beginningless supreme Brahman, said to be neither being nor non-being. With hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads, and faces everywhere, hearing everywhere in the world, it stands enveloping all. Appearing through the qualities of all the senses, yet free of all the senses; unattached, yet supporting all; free of the guṇas, yet the enjoyer of the guṇas—

---

### Devanagari
ज्ञेयं यत्तत्प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वाऽमृतमश्नुते।

अनादिमत्परं ब्रह्म न सत्तन्नासदुच्यते
सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत्सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम्।सर्वतः श्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति
सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम्।असक्तं सर्वभृच्चैव निर्गुणं गुणभोक्तृ च

### IAST
jñeyaṃ yattatpravakṣyāmi yajjñātvā'mṛtamaśnute|

anādimatparaṃ brahma na sattannāsaducyate
sarvataḥ pāṇipādaṃ tatsarvato'kṣiśiromukham|sarvataḥ śrutimalloke sarvamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati
sarvendriyaguṇābhāsaṃ sarvendriyavivarjitam|asaktaṃ sarvabhṛccaiva nirguṇaṃ guṇabhoktṛ ca

### Pratibha Translation
I will declare that which is to be known, knowing which one tastes immortality. It is the beginningless supreme Brahman, said to be neither being nor non-being. With hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads, and faces everywhere, hearing everywhere in the world, it stands enveloping all. Appearing through the qualities of all the senses, yet free of all the senses; unattached, yet supporting all; free of the guṇas, yet the enjoyer of the guṇas—

### Pratibha Commentary
The knowable is not another object in the field; it is Brahman, tasting which is immortality. The contested move is the double negation: na sat, na asat—neither being nor non-being as ordinarily conceived. This is not vagueness; it blocks capturing the Absolute with the categories that organize the field. Then the text pivots into cosmic body language: hands and feet everywhere, enveloping all—echoing the Puruṣa hymn and foreshadowing the theophany of chapter 11. The paradoxes intensify: sense-appearing yet sense-free, unattached yet all-supporting, nirguṇa yet guṇa-enjoyer. Knowledge here means holding non-dual tension without collapsing into pantheism or world-denial. Existentially, immortality is not postponed reward; it is the flavor (aśnute) of knowing that which cannot be boxed as a thing or a nothing.  Immortality as tasting (aśnute) matters: the knowable is not a diagram you assent to; it is a flavor that rearranges fear of death. Read as existential demand, the verse asks for a changed stance in the next difficult hour—not for ornamental agreement with a doctrine.

### Key Terms
**jñeya (ज्ञेय)** — the knowable -> Brahman as that knowing which yields immortality -> “object” wrongly implies ordinary objectivity.
**anādi (अनादि)** — beginningless -> without temporal origin -> “eternal” can still smuggle a long timeline.
**na sat / na asat (न सत् / न असत्)** — neither being nor non-being -> beyond ontic binaries of the field -> “mysterious” as a shrug misses the precise category-break.
**nirguṇa (निर्गुण)** — without guṇas -> free of prakṛtic strands -> “attributeless” can sound barren rather than unbound.
**guṇabhoktṛ (गुणभोक्तृ)** — enjoyer of the guṇas -> witness-enjoyer amid qualities without being bound as them -> “experiencer” can reinstall a needy ego.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad III.16–17]:** The all-limbed cosmic person resonates with sarvataḥ pāṇi-pāda imagery.
*Divergence:* Śvetāśvatara leans into Rudra-theism; the Gītā embeds the image inside a jñeya teaching tied to immortality.
**[Nāgārjuna, Mūlamadhyamakakārikā I / tetralemma]:** Refusal of naive being/non-being categories is structurally homologous.
*Divergence:* Nāgārjuna empties inherent existence; Krishna points to a supreme Brahman that is liveable as immortality.
**[Pseudo-Dionysius, Mystical Theology]:** God beyond affirmation and negation parallels na sat / na asat.
*Divergence:* Dionysius climbs by negation into divine darkness; Krishna simultaneously affirms cosmic pervasion and sensuous paradox.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Sit for ten minutes. On the in-breath: “not a thing.” On the out-breath: “not nothing.” Rest as the knowing in which both phrases appear.

## Near and Far, Undivided in the Divided
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 13.16–13.18

Outside and inside beings, the unmoving and the moving; because of its subtlety it is unknowable; it stands far away and also near. Undivided, yet standing as if divided in beings; that knowable is to be known as the supporter of beings, as devouring and as generating. That is the light of lights, said to be beyond darkness; knowledge, the knowable, and reachable by knowledge, dwelling in the heart of all.

---

### Devanagari
बहिरन्तश्च भूतानामचरं चरमेव च।सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थं चान्तिके च तत्
अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम्।भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च
ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते।ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य विष्ठितम्

### IAST
bahirantaśca bhūtānāmacaraṃ carameva ca|sūkṣmatvāttadavijñeyaṃ dūrasthaṃ cāntike ca tat
avibhaktaṃ ca bhūteṣu vibhaktamiva ca sthitam|bhūtabhartṛ ca tajjñeyaṃ grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca
jyotiṣāmapi tajjyotistamasaḥ paramucyate|jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānagamyaṃ hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam

### Pratibha Translation
Outside and inside beings, the unmoving and the moving; because of its subtlety it is unknowable; it stands far away and also near. Undivided, yet standing as if divided in beings; that knowable is to be known as the supporter of beings, as devouring and as generating. That is the light of lights, said to be beyond darkness; knowledge, the knowable, and reachable by knowledge, dwelling in the heart of all.

### Pratibha Commentary
The knowable is described by coincidence of opposites: outside/inside, still/moving, far/near, undivided/as-if-divided. Subtlety (sūkṣmatva) makes it “unknowable” to gross grasping while remaining heart-intimate. The contested claim is that unity appears as multiplicity without ceasing to be unity—“as if divided” (vibhaktam iva) is the hinge. Supporter, devourer, generator: the Absolute is not a quiet spectator only; it is the full cycle of manifestation. Then the verse names it light of lights beyond darkness, and collapses the triad: jñāna, jñeya, and jñānagamya—knowledge, knowable, and reachable by knowledge—dwelling in every heart. Existentially, this relocates the sacred from elsewhere to the hṛdaya, while warning that nearness does not equal easy possession.  Nearness without possession is the heart’s paradox: what dwells in all hearts cannot be clutched as a private object among other objects. Read as existential demand, the verse asks for a changed stance in the next difficult hour—not for ornamental agreement with a doctrine.

### Key Terms
**sūkṣmatva (सूक्ष्मत्व)** — subtlety -> fineness that escapes gross cognition -> “invisibility” is too crude.
**avibhakta / vibhakta iva (अविभक्त / विभक्त इव)** — undivided / as if divided -> non-dual presence appearing multiple -> “immanence” alone misses the “as if.”
**grasiṣṇu / prabhaviṣṇu (ग्रसिष्णु / प्रभविष्णु)** — devouring / generating -> cosmic withdrawal and emission -> “destroyer/creator” can sound mythic-external.
**jyotisām jyotiḥ (ज्योतिषां ज्योतिः)** — light of lights -> illumination that lights all lights -> “supreme light” can become a visualization fetish.
**hṛdi (हृदि)** — in the heart -> intimate locus of the knowable -> “emotion center” misses the Upaniṣadic heart as awareness-seat.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Īśā Upaniṣad 5]:** It moves and moves not, is far and near—near-exact structural homology.
*Divergence:* Īśā compresses into mantra density; the Gītā expands into supporter/devourer/generator and the jñāna triad.
**[Plotinus, Enneads V.1]:** The One present to the soul and yet beyond parallels near/far and light of lights.
*Divergence:* Plotinus prioritizes contemplative ascent; Krishna insists the knowable already dwells in all hearts.
**[Heart Sūtra]:** Form/emptiness paradoxes echo undivided-yet-as-if-divided.
*Divergence:* The Heart Sūtra empties inherent nature; the Gītā affirms a Brahman that is light, knowledge, and heart-dweller.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Look at three distinct people or objects. For each, silently say: “undivided, appearing as if divided.” Feel the difference between idea and seeing.

## Nature and Person Are Beginningless
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 13.19–13.21

Thus the field, knowledge, and the knowable have been spoken in summary. My devotee, knowing this, becomes fit for My state of being. Know that both nature [prakṛti] and the person [puruṣa] are beginningless. Know also that modifications and the guṇas are born of prakṛti. In the production of the body and the senses, prakṛti is said to be the cause; the person is said to be the cause in the experiencing of pleasure and pain.

---

### Devanagari
इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः।मद्भक्त एतद्विज्ञाय मद्भावायोपपद्यते
प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव विद्ध्यनादी उभावपि।विकारांश्च गुणांश्चैव विद्धि प्रकृतिसंभवान्
कार्यकारणकर्तृत्वे हेतुः प्रकृतिरुच्यते।पुरुषः सुखदुःखानां भोक्तृत्वे हेतुरुच्यते

### IAST
iti kṣetraṃ tathā jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ coktaṃ samāsataḥ|madbhakta etadvijñāya madbhāvāyopapadyate
prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva viddhyanādī ubhāvapi|vikārāṃśca guṇāṃścaiva viddhi prakṛtisaṃbhavān
kāryakāraṇakartṛtve hetuḥ prakṛtirucyate|puruṣaḥ sukhaduḥkhānāṃ bhoktṛtve heturucyate

### Pratibha Translation
Thus the field, knowledge, and the knowable have been spoken in summary. My devotee, knowing this, becomes fit for My state of being. Know that both nature [prakṛti] and the person [puruṣa] are beginningless. Know also that modifications and the guṇas are born of prakṛti. In the production of the body and the senses, prakṛti is said to be the cause; the person is said to be the cause in the experiencing of pleasure and pain.

### Pratibha Commentary
The summary seals a path: the devotee who knows this becomes fit for madbhāva—Krishna’s own mode of being. Knowledge is not terminal information; it is initiation into a shared ontological stance. Then the classical Sāṃkhya pair returns with a twist: both prakṛti and puruṣa are beginningless. The contested move assigns causality carefully: prakṛti causes the apparatus (body-senses), puruṣa causes bhoktṛtva—the tasting of pleasure and pain. Bondage is not that awareness exists, but that witnessing gets contracted into ownership of affect. Existentially, this explains why changing circumstances never ends suffering: as long as the person is entangled as enjoyer-owner, the field will keep delivering sukha-duḥkha to a claimant.  Distinguishing productivity from enjoyership is daily medicine: you can let prakṛti build the scene without signing the affect as identity. Read as existential demand, the verse asks for a changed stance in the next difficult hour—not for ornamental agreement with a doctrine. Read as existential demand, the verse asks for a changed stance in the next difficult hour—not for ornamental agreement with a doctrine.

### Key Terms
**madbhāva (मद्भाव)** — “My being / My state” -> participation in Krishna’s mode -> “my nature” as imitation misses ontological fittingness.
**anādi (अनादि)** — beginningless -> no first moment of prakṛti or puruṣa -> “always existed” can still temporalize wrongly.
**bhoktṛtva (भोक्तृत्व)** — enjoyership / experiencership -> puruṣa’s role in tasting affect -> “consumer” is too economic and crude.
**kārya-kāraṇa (कार्य-कारण)** — effect-cause complex -> prakṛti’s productivity of embodiment -> “causation” in physics misses yogic anthropology.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Sāṃkhya Kārikā 3, 19–21]:** Prakṛti as active, puruṣa as experiencer is near-direct homology.
*Divergence:* Sāṃkhya ends in isolation of puruṣa; the Gītā routes knowledge into madbhāva and devotion.
**[Augustine, Confessions X]:** Memory and desire as loci of enjoyment/suffering parallel bhoktṛtva’s centrality.
*Divergence:* Augustine heals enjoyership by ordering love to God; Krishna analyzes enjoyership as puruṣa’s causal role amid prakṛti.
**[Buddha, SN 12 (dependent origination)]:** Feeling and craving as binding nodes echo pleasure-pain enjoyership.
*Divergence:* Buddhism dismantles a permanent puruṣa; the Gītā retains puruṣa while relocating bondage to misidentified enjoyership.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
At the next spike of pleasure or pain, say: “Prakṛti produced the event; enjoyership is claiming it.” Rest one minute without feeding the claim.
