## Take Refuge, Do All Actions, Become Mind-Mine
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 18.56–18.58

Even while always performing all actions, taking refuge in Me, one attains by My grace the eternal, imperishable station. Mentally renouncing all actions in Me, intent on Me, taking refuge in buddhi-yoga, be conscious of Me continually. Conscious of Me, you will cross all difficulties by My grace; but if from egoism you will not listen, you will perish.

---

### Devanagari
सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः।मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम्
चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः।बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव
मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि।अथ चेत्त्वमहङ्कारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि

### IAST
sarvakarmāṇyapi sadā kurvāṇo madvyapāśrayaḥ|matprasādādavāpnoti śāśvataṃ padamavyayam
cetasā sarvakarmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya matparaḥ|buddhiyogamupāśritya maccittaḥ satataṃ bhava
maccittaḥ sarvadurgāṇi matprasādāttariṣyasi|atha cettvamahaṅkārānna śroṣyasi vinaṅkṣyasi

### Pratibha Translation
Even while always performing all actions, taking refuge in Me, one attains by My grace the eternal, imperishable station. Mentally renouncing all actions in Me, intent on Me, taking refuge in buddhi-yoga, be conscious of Me continually. Conscious of Me, you will cross all difficulties by My grace; but if from egoism you will not listen, you will perish.

### Pratibha Commentary
The path becomes simultaneously active and surrendered: do all actions, take refuge, receive prasāda, attain the eternal pada. Mentally renounce actions into Krishna, practice buddhi-yoga, become maccitta. Grace carries across difficulties; egoistic non-listening leads to ruin. The contested braid is grace and discipline, action and mental saṃnyāsa. Existentially, “I’ll listen later” is already the ahaṅkāra warning. The next verses will show that even refusal is still prakṛti’s enlistment. In the Gītā’s pedagogy, concept without existential cut becomes another ornament of bondage; therefore the verse must be read as a demand on perception, desire, and refuge, not as a museum label on a doctrine. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics.

### Key Terms
**madvyapāśraya (मद्व्यपाश्रय)** — taking refuge in Me -> condition while acting -> 'inspiration' is thinner.
**matprasāda (मत्प्रसाद)** — My grace/favor -> means of attaining the station and crossing difficulties -> 'luck' erases relation.
**maccitta (मच्चित्त)** — mind/heart on Me -> continual consciousness of Krishna -> 'thinking about religion' understates.
**ahaṅkārāt na śroṣyasi (अहङ्कारात् न श्रोष्यसि)** — from egoism you will not listen -> ruin’s cause -> 'independence' may be its flattering name.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Gītā 9.22 / 9.34]:** Refuge and mind-fixed-on-Me continue.
*Divergence:* 18.56–58 add grace-crossing and the warning of egoistic deafness.
**[Paul on grace and working]:** Grace with ongoing action resonates cautiously.
*Divergence:* Pauline justification debates differ; here prasāda and buddhi-yoga are yogic-bhakti.
**[Augustine on grace and listening]:** Refusal to hear as ruin resonates.
*Divergence:* Augustine’s grace is Christic; Krishna speaks as the refuge and the grace-giver.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Begin work by mentally placing actions in the Lord. When ego says 'I won’t listen,' name the peril and return to maccitta for one minute.

## Nature Will Enlist You Anyway
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 18.59–18.60

If, taking refuge in egoism, you think 'I will not fight,' this resolve of yours is vain; nature will compel you. Bound by your own action born of nature, O son of Kuntī, you will helplessly do even that which you do not wish to do from delusion.

---

### Devanagari
यदहङ्कारमाश्रित्य न योत्स्य इति मन्यसे।मिथ्यैष व्यवसायस्ते प्रकृतिस्त्वां नियोक्ष्यति
स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा।कर्तुं नेच्छसि यन्मोहात्करिष्यस्यवशोऽपि तत्

### IAST
yadahaṅkāramāśritya na yotsya iti manyase|mithyaiṣa vyavasāyaste prakṛtistvāṃ niyokṣyati
svabhāvajena kaunteya nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā|kartuṃ necchasi yanmohātkariṣyasyavaśo'pi tat

### Pratibha Translation
If, taking refuge in egoism, you think 'I will not fight,' this resolve of yours is vain; nature will compel you. Bound by your own action born of nature, O son of Kuntī, you will helplessly do even that which you do not wish to do from delusion.

### Pratibha Commentary
The psychology of refusal is unmasked. “I will not fight,” if rooted in ahaṅkāra, is mithyā vyavasāya—vain resolve—because prakṛti will appoint you (niyokṣyati). Bound by svabhāva-born karma, you will do even what moha refuses. The contested claim attacks spiritualized avoidance: your “no” may still be nature’s “yes” in disguise. Existentially, this is terrifying and freeing. Terrifying: escape theater fails. Freeing: the fantasy of a pure veto outside nature is dropped, preparing true śaraṇa. In the Gītā’s pedagogy, concept without existential cut becomes another ornament of bondage; therefore the verse must be read as a demand on perception, desire, and refuge, not as a museum label on a doctrine. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics.

### Key Terms
**mithyā vyavasāya (मिथ्या व्यवसाय)** — false/vain resolve -> egoic refusal -> 'boundary' can be real or this.
**prakṛtiḥ niyokṣyati (प्रकृतिः नियोक्ष्यति)** — nature will appoint/compel -> inevitability under svabhāva -> 'determinism' as abstract thesis misses the pastoral sting.
**avaśaḥ (अवशः)** — helpless / not in control -> how the unwanted is done -> 'victim' is inexact; it is nature-binding.
**svabhāvaja karma (स्वभावज कर्म)** — action born of nature -> the binding specific -> 'habits' is partial.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Gītā 3.33]:** Even the wise act according to nature—continuity.
*Divergence:* 18.59–60 apply it to Arjuna’s war-refusal as vain ego-resolve.
**[Spinoza on illusion of free veto]:** Thinking we veto while determined resonates.
*Divergence:* Spinoza’s God/nature differs; Krishna prepares surrender to the heart-Lord.
**[Freud / unconscious compulsion (loose)]:** Doing what we think we refuse resonates psychologically.
*Divergence:* Psychoanalysis is secular; here prakṛti and moha are the frame.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Find one 'I will never' that keeps happening anyway. Confess it as nature-binding, then seek refuge rather than a louder veto.

## The Lord Turns Beings Like a Machine
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 18.61

The Lord dwells in the heart-region of all beings, O Arjuna, causing all beings to turn by His māyā, as if mounted on a machine.

---

### Devanagari
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति।भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया

### IAST
īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛddeśe'rjuna tiṣṭhati|bhrāmayansarvabhūtāni yantrārūḍhāni māyayā

### Pratibha Translation
The Lord dwells in the heart-region of all beings, O Arjuna, causing all beings to turn by His māyā, as if mounted on a machine.

### Pratibha Commentary
One of the Gītā’s most exact images: Īśvara seated in the hṛd-deśa turns all beings by māyā as if yantrārūḍha—mounted on a machine. The contested claim intensifies 18.59–60: compulsion is not blind nature only; it is the Lord’s māyā-engine. Existentially, this can crush or liberate. Crush if heard as cosmic sadism. Liberate if heard as the end of the fantasy that you are the sole engineer. The next verse will convert the image into refuge. In the Gītā’s pedagogy, concept without existential cut becomes another ornament of bondage; therefore the verse must be read as a demand on perception, desire, and refuge, not as a museum label on a doctrine. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics.

### Key Terms
**hṛd-deśa (हृद्देश)** — heart-region -> Lord’s dwelling -> 'feelings' psychologizes.
**bhrāmayan (भ्रामयन्)** — causing to turn/wander -> divine turning of beings -> 'manipulation' is the suspicious mishearing.
**yantrārūḍha (यन्त्रारूढ)** — mounted on a machine -> image of driven turning -> 'puppet' is harsher than the text’s pastoral aim.
**māyā (माया)** — measuring power / wondrous artifice -> means of turning -> 'illusion' alone understates agency.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Gītā 15.15 / heart-dweller]:** Indwelling continues into machine-turning image.
*Divergence:* 18.61 makes the turning explicit via māyā.
**[Plotinus on the One’s presence to souls]:** Inner turning source resonates loosely.
*Divergence:* Plotinus avoids personal machine imagery; Krishna is starkly theistic-mechanical in metaphor.
**[Calvinist providence debates (contrast)]:** Divine governance of actions resonates and diverges.
*Divergence:* Productive divergence: Gītā’s image prepares śaraṇa, not merely decree-speculation.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Sit hand on heart. Contemplate: 'The turner dwells here.' Let panic and pride both soften without becoming passive cruelty toward others.

## Go to Him Alone for Refuge
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 18.62

Go to Him alone for refuge with your whole being, O Bhārata. By His grace you will attain supreme peace and the eternal station.

---

### Devanagari
तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत।तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम्

### IAST
tameva śaraṇaṃ gaccha sarvabhāvena bhārata|tatprasādātparāṃ śāntiṃ sthānaṃ prāpsyasi śāśvatam

### Pratibha Translation
Go to Him alone for refuge with your whole being, O Bhārata. By His grace you will attain supreme peace and the eternal station.

### Pratibha Commentary
The machine-image flips into invitation: tameva śaraṇaṃ gaccha sarva-bhāvena—go to Him alone as refuge with your whole being. Grace yields parā śānti and śāśvata sthāna. The contested simplicity after complex teaching is intentional. Analysis ends in refuge. Existentially, partial refuge—God plus career-as-savior plus image-as-savior—fails sarva-bhāva. Whole-being means the parts stop running rival shelters. In the Gītā’s pedagogy, concept without existential cut becomes another ornament of bondage; therefore the verse must be read as a demand on perception, desire, and refuge, not as a museum label on a doctrine. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics.

### Key Terms
**śaraṇaṃ gaccha (शरणं गच्छ)** — go to refuge -> imperative of surrender -> 'seek comfort' understates.
**sarva-bhāvena (सर्वभावेन)** — with one’s whole being -> total refuge -> 'very sincerely' is weaker.
**tat-prasādāt (तत्प्रसादात्)** — by His grace -> means of peace and station -> 'after asking nicely' trivializes.
**śāśvatam sthānam (शाश्वतं स्थानम्)** — eternal station -> goal of refuge -> 'safe place' softens.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Gītā 9.32–34 / 18.56]:** Refuge and grace continuity.
*Divergence:* 18.62 is the clean imperative after the heart-machine verse.
**[Psalm 46 / God as refuge]:** Whole-being refuge and peace resonate.
*Divergence:* Psalmic covenant frame differs; structure is grace-peace-refuge.
**[Śaraṇāgati in Śrīvaiṣṇava reception]:** This verse is classic refuge theology.
*Divergence:* Later doctrinal elaborations differ; the text’s force is total-bhāva refuge.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Speak aloud once: 'I go to You alone for refuge with my whole being.' Then notice which rival refuge protests—and include it in the offering.

## Deliberate, Then Do as You Will
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 18.63

Thus knowledge more secret than secret has been declared by Me to you. Having reflected on it completely, do as you wish.

---

### Devanagari
इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया।विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु

### IAST
iti te jñānamākhyātaṃ guhyādguhyataraṃ mayā|vimṛśyaitadaśeṣeṇa yathecchasi tathā kuru

### Pratibha Translation
Thus knowledge more secret than secret has been declared by Me to you. Having reflected on it completely, do as you wish.

### Pratibha Commentary
After command, freedom: vimṛśya etat aśeṣeṇa yathecchasi tathā kuru—reflect fully, then do as you wish. The contested generosity refuses brainwashing. The most secret knowledge is given, then returned to Arjuna’s icchā. Existentially, this is adult spiritual pedagogy. Contemplation is required; coercion is refused. The following verses will intensify love’s secret, but not by canceling this freedom. In the Gītā’s pedagogy, concept without existential cut becomes another ornament of bondage; therefore the verse must be read as a demand on perception, desire, and refuge, not as a museum label on a doctrine. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics.

### Key Terms
**guhyād guhyataram (गुह्याद् गुह्यतरम्)** — more secret than secret -> intensified disclosure -> 'esoteric flex' misuses it.
**vimṛśya (विमृश्य)** — having reflected/deliberated -> required before action -> 'overthink' is the parody.
**yathecchasi tathā kuru (यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु)** — do as you wish -> returned freedom -> 'anything goes' ignores the reflection requirement.
**aśeṣeṇa (अशेषेण)** — completely / without remainder -> thorough reflection -> 'skim the vibe' fails.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Kantian autonomy (loose)]:** Reflect then act as free agent resonates partially.
*Divergence:* Kant’s law differs; here reflection is on disclosed divine knowledge.
**[Benedict’s abbot counsel then free assent structures]:** Hearing, considering, acting resonates.
*Divergence:* Monastic obedience frames differ; Krishna explicitly returns icchā to Arjuna.
**[Gītā 18.59–60 tension]:** Nature binds, yet do as you wish—productive paradox.
*Divergence:* Freedom is not outside prakṛti; it is reflective response to revelation.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Take one teaching from this chapter. Reflect for ten uninterrupted minutes. Only then choose an act—without outsourcing the choice to impulse or to a guru-voice in your head.

## Listen Again: You Are Deeply Loved
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 18.64

Hear again My supreme word, the most secret of all. You are dearly loved by Me; therefore I will speak what is good for you.

---

### Devanagari
सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः श्रृणु मे परमं वचः।इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम्

Hear again My supreme word, the most secret of all. You are dearly loved by Me; therefore I will speak what is good for you.

Before the final imperatives, love speaks: iṣṭo’si me dṛḍham—you are firmly beloved to Me; therefore I speak hitam, what benefits you. The contested tenderness matters. The Gītā’s hardest commands are framed as friendship’s good, not domination’s thrill. Existentially, receive this before 18.65–66. Refuge is easier to hear from love than from threat. If you only hear cosmic machine and not belovedness, you are still missing the most secret word’s tone. In the Gītā’s pedagogy, concept without existential cut becomes another ornament of bondage; therefore the verse must be read as a demand on perception, desire, and refuge, not as a museum label on a doctrine. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics.

### Key Terms
**sarva-guhyatama (सर्वगुह्यतम)** — most secret of all -> supreme disclosure -> 'final secret tip' cheapens.
**iṣṭo’si me (इष्टोऽसि मे)** — you are beloved to Me -> affection as basis of teaching -> 'God likes me' as ego-boost fails the dṛḍham.
**dṛḍham (दृढम्)** — firmly -> intensity of love -> 'kinda care' is not this.
**hitam (हितम्)** — beneficial good -> content of the supreme word -> 'nice advice' understates.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[John 15 on friendship and command]:** Love framing hard command resonates.
*Divergence:* Christic friendship differs; structure is love-then-imperative.
**[Gītā 4.3 / 10.1]:** Teaching given because of love/devotion continues.
*Divergence:* 18.64 makes belovedness the explicit reason for the final secret.
**[Sufi beloved-speech]:** Truth spoken from love’s nearness resonates.
*Divergence:* Sufi fanā frames differ; here the beloved is Arjuna and the speaker is Krishna.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Sit and receive, without producing: 'You are firmly dear to Me.' Notice resistance. Stay until the nervous system hears benefit, not flattery.

## Become Mind-Mine, My Devotee, My Worshipper
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 18.65

Become one whose mind is on Me, My devotee, My worshipper; bow to Me. You will come to Me alone; I promise you truly, for you are dear to Me.

---

### Devanagari
मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु।मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे

### Pratibha Commentary
Four imperatives densify the path: manmanā, madbhakta, madyājī, mām namaskuru—mind on Me, My devotee, My worshipper, bow to Me. Promise: māmevaiṣyasi—you will come to Me alone; satyaṃ te pratijāne—I vow it truly; because priyo’si me. The contested density is practical: cognition, love, ritual offering, and embodied bow are one package. Existentially, pick the missing limb. The vow is not a loophole around practice; it is love’s certainty that practice’s orientation reaches Him. In the Gītā’s pedagogy, concept without existential cut becomes another ornament of bondage; therefore the verse must be read as a demand on perception, desire, and refuge, not as a museum label on a doctrine. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics.

### Key Terms
**manmanā (मन्मनाः)** — mind/heart Mine -> first imperative -> 'thinking of God occasionally' is weaker.
**madyājī (मद्याजी)** — My worshipper/sacrificer -> ritual offering to Krishna -> 'grateful vibes' understates.
**pratijāne (प्रतिजाने)** — I promise/vow -> divine assurance -> 'optimistic wish' erases vow-force.
**māmevaiṣyasi (मामेवैष्यसि)** — you will come to Me alone -> exclusive arrival -> 'feel close' is thinner.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Gītā 9.34]:** Near-identical imperative cluster returns as climax.
*Divergence:* 18.65 adds explicit vow and belovedness.
**[Shema / whole-love commands]:** Total orientation of mind and devotion resonates.
*Divergence:* Jewish covenantal monotheism differs; structure is total love-obedience.
**[Nārada Bhakti Sūtra on primary devotion]:** Devotion as primary means resonates.
*Divergence:* Nāradīya centers bhakti’s sweetness; here vow and bow complete the cluster.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Practice the four in order once: set mind, awaken devotion, make a small offering, bow with the body. Do it without asking for a mood-reward.

## Abandon All Dharmas: Take Refuge in Me Alone
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 18.66

Abandoning all dharmas, take refuge in Me alone. I will liberate you from all evils; do not grieve.

---

### Devanagari
सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज।अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः

### IAST
sarvadharmānparityajya māmekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja|ahaṃ tvā sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ

### Pratibha Translation
Abandoning all dharmas, take refuge in Me alone. I will liberate you from all evils; do not grieve.

### Pratibha Commentary
This is the Gītā’s razor. Sarva-dharmān parityajya māmekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja—having abandoned all dharmas, go to Me alone as refuge. Then the vow: ahaṃ tvā sarva-pāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi—I will liberate you from all evils/sins; mā śucaḥ—do not grieve. The contested move is not antinomian vandalism of ethics; it is the end of salvation-by-portfolio. “All dharmas” includes the righteous projects by which the ego still seeks to secure itself—varṇa-duty as self-justification, renunciation as self-justification, even “Gītā practice” as self-justification. The verse does not license cruelty; it dethrones rival refuges. After eighteen chapters of discrimination, guṇas, svadharma, and tapas, Krishna says the last act is not another technique but exclusive śaraṇa. Theologically, agency shifts: mokṣa is promised in the first person by the Lord. Pastorally, the battlefield grief that opened the Gītā is addressed at the root: do not grieve—not because the field is unreal only, but because refuge holds. Existentially, find what you are still clutching as co-savior beside the Lord—your correctness, your wound, your role, your metaphysics—and let the verse pry it open. The fear that abandoning all dharmas means becoming lawless is itself often a dharma-idol’s voice. True refuge produces a life; it does not need a side-altar of self-rescue. When this verse is heard only as slogan, it becomes cheap. When heard after 18.63–65’s freedom, love, and vow, it becomes the end of bargaining.

### Key Terms
**sarva-dharmān parityajya (सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य)** — abandoning all dharmas -> dropping all rival duty-refuges -> 'be unethical' is the catastrophic misreading.
**mām ekam (मामेकम्)** — Me alone -> exclusivity of refuge -> 'mostly God' fails eka.
**sarva-pāpebhyaḥ (सर्वपापेभ्यः)** — from all evils/sins -> scope of promised liberation -> 'bad vibes' trivializes.
**mokṣayiṣyāmi (मोक्षयिष्यामि)** — I will liberate -> first-person future of the Lord -> 'you'll get free somehow' erases the vow.
**mā śucaḥ (मा शुचः)** — do not grieve -> pastoral command closing Arjuna’s wound -> 'cheer up' is insultingly thin.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Luke 15 / lost and found grace]:** Liberation from the burden of self-justifying righteousness resonates.
*Divergence:* Christian grace is Christic; here exclusive refuge in Krishna is the liberating vow.
**[Śaraṇāgati / prapatti traditions]:** This verse is the locus classicus of total surrender.
*Divergence:* School differences on conditions remain; the textual force is eka-śaraṇa plus divine mokṣa-vow.
**[Paul, Philippians 3 on counting credentials loss]:** Abandoning dharma-credentials for the One resonates structurally.
*Divergence:* Paul’s Christ-gain differs; both dethrone religious self-security.
**[Gītā 2.7 / 18.73 arc]:** From Arjuna’s helpless refuge-ask to grief’s end completes the pedagogy.
*Divergence:* 2.7 asks for śiṣya-refuge; 18.66 answers with absolute śaraṇa and mā śucaḥ.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Write down three 'dharmas' you use to save yourself (roles, correctness, practices-as-proof). Physically set the paper down and say: 'Refuge in You alone. Do not let me make these co-saviors.' Sit in the fear until it softens into trust.

## Who May Hear, Who Must Speak
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 18.67–18.69

This is never to be spoken by you to one without austerity, nor to one without devotion, nor to one who does not want to listen, nor to one who resents Me. The one who teaches this supreme secret to My devotees, having shown highest devotion to Me, will come to Me without doubt. And no one among humans does what is more dear to Me than he, nor will there be another on earth dearer to Me than he.

---

### Devanagari
इदं ते नातपस्काय नाभक्ताय कदाचन।न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति
य इमं परमं गुह्यं मद्भक्तेष्वभिधास्यति।भक्ितं मयि परां कृत्वा मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयः
न च तस्मान्मनुष्येषु कश्िचन्मे प्रियकृत्तमः।भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि

### IAST
idaṃ te nātapaskāya nābhaktāya kadācana|na cāśuśrūṣave vācyaṃ na ca māṃ yo'bhyasūyati
ya imaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ madbhakteṣvabhidhāsyati|bhakitaṃ mayi parāṃ kṛtvā māmevaiṣyatyasaṃśayaḥ
na ca tasmānmanuṣyeṣu kaśicanme priyakṛttamaḥ|bhavitā na ca me tasmādanyaḥ priyataro bhuvi

### Pratibha Translation
This is never to be spoken by you to one without austerity, nor to one without devotion, nor to one who does not want to listen, nor to one who resents Me. The one who teaches this supreme secret to My devotees, having shown highest devotion to Me, will come to Me without doubt. And no one among humans does what is more dear to Me than he, nor will there be another on earth dearer to Me than he.

### Pratibha Commentary
After the open razor, a gate: the teaching is not for the atapas, abhakta, aśuśrūṣu, or the resentful. Then the highest human dearness: teaching this secret to devotees is the most priyakṛt toward Krishna. The contested pair is generosity and protection. Existentially, this warns against dumping 18.66 into contemptuous ears as debate-fuel, and it dignifies responsible transmission as love’s labor. In the Gītā’s pedagogy, concept without existential cut becomes another ornament of bondage; therefore the verse must be read as a demand on perception, desire, and refuge, not as a museum label on a doctrine. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics.

### Key Terms
**na atapaskāya (नातपस्काय)** — not to the non-austere -> fitness for hearing -> 'gatekeeping' can be faithful or egoic.
**aśuśrūṣu (अशुश्रूषु)** — one who does not wish to hear -> unwilling listener -> 'skeptic' is not always this.
**abhyasūyati (अभ्यसूयति)** — resents/envies Me -> barred hearer -> 'critical thinker' is not identical with resentment.
**priyakṛttama (प्रियकृत्तम)** — most dear-doer -> teacher of the secret to devotees -> 'influencer' is a parody.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Matthew 7 on pearls]:** Not casting sacred teaching recklessly resonates.
*Divergence:* Matthew’s frame differs; both protect holy speech from contempt.
**[Upaniṣadic adhikāra]:** Qualification for teaching/hearing is traditional homology.
*Divergence:* The Gītā centers bhakti and non-resentment explicitly.
**[Gītā 4.34]:** Approach knowers with humility—complement to this transmission ethic.
*Divergence:* 4.34 is for seekers; 18.67–69 for teachers’ responsibility and reward.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Before sharing a sacred teaching, check for austerity, devotion, willingness, and non-resentment in the field. If absent, practice silence as devotion.

## Study, Faithful Hearing, and the Lord’s Question
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 18.70–18.72

And the one who will study this dialogue of ours on dharma—by that sacrifice of knowledge I am worshipped; so I hold. And the person of faith who does not resent, even if he only hears—he too, liberated, attains the auspicious worlds of the meritorious. Has this been heard by you, O Pārtha, with one-pointed mind? Has your confusion born of ignorance been destroyed, O Dhanañjaya?

---

### Devanagari
अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः।ज्ञानयज्ञेन तेनाहमिष्टः स्यामिति मे मतिः
श्रद्धावाननसूयश्च श्रृणुयादपि यो नरः।सोऽपि मुक्तः शुभाँल्लोकान्प्राप्नुयात्पुण्यकर्मणाम्
कच्चिदेतच्छ्रुतं पार्थ त्वयैकाग्रेण चेतसा।कच्चिदज्ञानसंमोहः प्रनष्टस्ते धनञ्जय

### IAST
adhyeṣyate ca ya imaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃvādamāvayoḥ|jñānayajñena tenāhamiṣṭaḥ syāmiti me matiḥ
śraddhāvānanasūyaśca śrṛṇuyādapi yo naraḥ|so'pi muktaḥ śubhā~llokānprāpnuyātpuṇyakarmaṇām
kaccidetacchrutaṃ pārtha tvayaikāgreṇa cetasā|kaccidajñānasaṃmohaḥ pranaṣṭaste dhanañjaya

### Pratibha Translation
And the one who will study this dialogue of ours on dharma—by that sacrifice of knowledge I am worshipped; so I hold. And the person of faith who does not resent, even if he only hears—he too, liberated, attains the auspicious worlds of the meritorious. Has this been heard by you, O Pārtha, with one-pointed mind? Has your confusion born of ignorance been destroyed, O Dhanañjaya?

### Pratibha Commentary
Reception itself becomes yajña: studying the dharmya saṃvāda is jñāna-yajña by which Krishna is worshipped. Even faithful, non-resentful hearing liberates toward auspicious worlds. Then the intimate exam: kaccit—has it been heard with ekāgra mind? Has ajñāna-saṃmoha been destroyed? The contested pastoral genius ends philosophy with a question, not a threat. Existentially, the Gītā asks you the same. Not “Did you enjoy the aesthetics?” but “Is the delusion gone?” In the Gītā’s pedagogy, concept without existential cut becomes another ornament of bondage; therefore the verse must be read as a demand on perception, desire, and refuge, not as a museum label on a doctrine. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics.

### Key Terms
**jñāna-yajña (ज्ञानयज्ञ)** — sacrifice of knowledge -> study as worship -> 'content consumption' fails.
**śraddhāvān anasūyaḥ (श्रद्धावाननसूयः)** — faithful and non-resentful -> hearer’s qualifications -> 'spiritual fan' understates.
**ekāgreṇa cetasā (एकाग्रेण चेतसा)** — with one-pointed mind -> quality of hearing -> 'multitasking podcast spirituality' fails.
**ajñāna-saṃmoha (अज्ञानसंमोह)** — confusion/delusion born of ignorance -> what must be destroyed -> 'stress' is thinner.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Gītā 4.28 / knowledge sacrifice]:** Jñāna-yajña continues.
*Divergence:* 18.70 makes study of this dialogue itself that sacrifice.
**[Shema’s 'hear']:** Hearing as covenantal act resonates.
*Divergence:* Jewish hearing is Torah-shaped; here hearing is of the Krishna-Arjuna saṃvāda.
**[Socratic elenchus ending in question]:** Philosophical care ending with examination resonates.
*Divergence:* Socrates frees by question; Krishna asks whether delusion is already destroyed.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Answer Krishna’s questions in writing: Did I hear one-pointedly? What delusion remains? Be concrete; do not perform 'yes.'

## My Delusion Is Gone; I Will Do Your Word
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 18.73–18.75

Arjuna said: My delusion is gone; memory is regained by Your grace, O Acyuta. I stand firm, with doubts gone; I will do Your word. Sañjaya said: Thus I heard this wondrous, hair-raising dialogue of Vāsudeva and the great-souled Pārtha. By Vyāsa’s grace I heard this supreme secret, yoga from the Lord of yoga, Kṛṣṇa himself speaking.

---

### Devanagari
अर्जुन उवाचनष्टो मोहः स्मृतिर्लब्धा त्वत्प्रसादान्मयाच्युत।स्थितोऽस्मि गतसन्देहः करिष्ये वचनं तव
सञ्जय उवाचइत्यहं वासुदेवस्य पार्थस्य च महात्मनः।संवादमिममश्रौषमद्भुतं रोमहर्षणम्
व्यासप्रसादाच्छ्रुतवानेतद्गुह्यमहं परम्।योगं योगेश्वरात्कृष्णात्साक्षात्कथयतः स्वयम्

### IAST
arjuna uvācanaṣṭo mohaḥ smṛtirlabdhā tvatprasādānmayācyuta|sthito'smi gatasandehaḥ kariṣye vacanaṃ tava
sañjaya uvācaityahaṃ vāsudevasya pārthasya ca mahātmanaḥ|saṃvādamimamaśrauṣamadbhutaṃ romaharṣaṇam
vyāsaprasādācchrutavānetadguhyamahaṃ param|yogaṃ yogeśvarātkṛṣṇātsākṣātkathayataḥ svayam

### Pratibha Translation
Arjuna said: My delusion is gone; memory is regained by Your grace, O Acyuta. I stand firm, with doubts gone; I will do Your word. Sañjaya said: Thus I heard this wondrous, hair-raising dialogue of Vāsudeva and the great-souled Pārtha. By Vyāsa’s grace I heard this supreme secret, yoga from the Lord of yoga, Kṛṣṇa himself speaking.

### Pratibha Commentary
Arjuna’s response is the pedagogical proof: naṣṭo mohaḥ, smṛtir labdhā, gata-sandehaḥ, kariṣye vacanaṃ tava—delusion destroyed, memory gained, doubt gone, I will do your word. Grace is credited (tvat-prasādāt). Then Sañjaya frames the hearing as adbhuta and romaharṣaṇa, received by Vyāsa’s grace from Yogesvara himself. The contested completeness is ethical: knowledge ends in kariṣye—I will do. Existentially, if your “realization” does not become vacana-performance, it is not yet Arjuna’s hearing. In the Gītā’s pedagogy, concept without existential cut becomes another ornament of bondage; therefore the verse must be read as a demand on perception, desire, and refuge, not as a museum label on a doctrine. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics.

### Key Terms
**naṣṭo mohaḥ (नष्टो मोहः)** — delusion destroyed -> Arjuna’s attainment -> 'I feel better' is not enough.
**smṛtir labdhā (स्मृतिर्लब्धा)** — memory regained -> recollection of truth/self -> 'recall facts' understates.
**kariṣye vacanam (करिष्ये वचनम्)** — I will do your word -> obedience as fruition -> 'agree intellectually' fails.
**yogeśvara (योगेश्वर)** — Lord of yoga -> Krishna as source of the heard yoga -> 'yoga teacher' is comic understatement.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Gītā 2.7 to 18.73]:** From collapse to standing firm completes the arc.
*Divergence:* The transformation is explicitly prasāda-caused.
**[Mary’s fiat / 'let it be']:** Hearing into doing resonates.
*Divergence:* Christian fiat is Incarnation-shaped; Arjuna’s fiat returns him to dharma-war under refuge.
**[Plato’s cave prisoner returning]:** Seeing then acting in the world resonates.
*Divergence:* Plato’s return is philosophical-political; Arjuna’s is obedient action under grace.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Make one kariṣye concrete: name the word you will do within twenty-four hours. Do it without renegotiating.

## Wherever There Is Krishna and Arjuna
**Source:** Bhagavad Gītā 18.76–18.78

O King, remembering again and again this wondrous and holy dialogue of Keśava and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again. And remembering again and again that most wondrous form of Hari, great is my amazement, O King, and I rejoice again and again. Wherever there is Kṛṣṇa, Lord of yoga, and wherever there is Pārtha, the archer—there, I hold, are fortune, victory, thriving, and lasting policy.

---

### Devanagari
राजन्संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य संवादमिममद्भुतम्।केशवार्जुनयोः पुण्यं हृष्यामि च मुहुर्मुहुः
तच्च संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य रूपमत्यद्भुतं हरेः।

विस्मयो मे महान् राजन् हृष्यामि च पुनः पुनः
यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः।

तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम

### IAST
rājansaṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya saṃvādamimamadbhutam|keśavārjunayoḥ puṇyaṃ hṛṣyāmi ca muhurmuhuḥ
tacca saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya rūpamatyadbhutaṃ hareḥ|

vismayo me mahān rājan hṛṣyāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ
yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇo yatra pārtho dhanurdharaḥ|

tatra śrīrvijayo bhūtirdhruvā nītirmatirmama

### Pratibha Translation
O King, remembering again and again this wondrous and holy dialogue of Keśava and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again. And remembering again and again that most wondrous form of Hari, great is my amazement, O King, and I rejoice again and again. Wherever there is Kṛṣṇa, Lord of yoga, and wherever there is Pārtha, the archer—there, I hold, are fortune, victory, thriving, and lasting policy.

### Pratibha Commentary
Sañjaya’s coda is liturgical memory: saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya—remembering again and again—the dialogue and the cosmic form, he rejoices. Then the final maxim: where Yogesvara Krishna and archer Arjuna are, there are śrī, vijaya, bhūti, and dhruvā nīti. The contested claim is not sports-team theology; it is that victory’s ecology is the conjunction of the Lord of yoga and the devoted doer of the word. Existentially, seek that conjunction, not isolated technique or isolated aggression. The Gītā ends not with withdrawal from the field but with a criterion for where thriving truly stands. In the Gītā’s pedagogy, concept without existential cut becomes another ornament of bondage; therefore the verse must be read as a demand on perception, desire, and refuge, not as a museum label on a doctrine. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics. The existential stake is that this teaching must change how you inhabit the next hour, not only how you narrate metaphysics.

### Key Terms
**saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya (संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य)** — remembering again and again -> joy’s engine -> 'nostalgia' understates living recollection.
**yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇaḥ (योगेश्वरः कृष्णः)** — Krishna, Lord of yoga -> one pole of victory’s presence -> 'god on our side' is the corrupt hearing.
**pārtho dhanurdharaḥ (पार्थो धनुर्धरः)** — Pārtha the bow-bearer -> devoted actor pole -> 'heroic ego' is the corrupt hearing.
**dhruvā nīti (ध्रुवा नीति)** — lasting right policy/conduct -> fruit of that conjunction -> 'winning strategy' can be amoral counterfeit.
**śrīr vijayo bhūtiḥ (श्रीर्विजयो भूतिः)** — fortune, victory, thriving -> signs of the conjunction -> 'success gospel' is the danger.

### Cross-Tradition Resonances
**[Gītā 11 remembered]:** Sañjaya’s amaze at the form ties back to theophany.
*Divergence:* The ending pairs form-memory with dialogue-memory as twin joys.
**[Exodus / 'God with us' victory motifs]:** Divine presence as victory condition resonates.
*Divergence:* Biblical holy war frames differ; here presence is Krishna-plus-Arjuna specifically.
**[Mahābhārata’s dharma-war horizon]:** The verse places the Gītā back into the epic’s stakes.
*Divergence:* Sañjaya speaks to Dhṛtarāṣṭra: the theological criterion implicitly judges the Kaurava project.

### Practice (Abhyasa)
Ask of your current struggle: 'Is the Lord of yoga present here—and am I present as one who will do the word?' If one pole is missing, restore it before seeking victory.
